passages.quote: In my life, I have had this happen numerous times.
passages.about: changing themselves to fit in

passages.quote: I catch myself changing who I am to fit in.
passages.about: habitually changing identity to fit in

passages.quote: The one significant time in my life I noticed me playing a role to make people like me, and I had to become a completely different person.
passages.about: playing a role to make friends

passages.quote: This time in my life was my freshman year of high school.
passages.about: acting differently during freshman year

passages.quote: I had these friends from middle school who were considered popular kids.
passages.about: having popular middle school friends

passages.quote: I tried so hard to change who I am to fit in with them, and it worked.
passages.about: changing behavior to fit in

passages.quote: I had them all fooled that I was exactly like them, a kid that pushed their parent's boundaries.
passages.about: pretending to push parental boundaries

passages.quote: I eventually had to give up the role.
passages.about: stopping the pretend persona

passages.quote: It became too much to handle.
passages.about: feeling overwhelmed by the act

passages.quote: I could not put up with the act anymore, so I dropped it.
passages.about: dropping the fake persona

passages.quote: This action caused me to lose many friends, but it was the best thing for my mental health.
passages.about: losing friends after dropping the act

passages.quote: It allowed me to become my authentic self again.
passages.about: returning to their authentic self

passages.quote: Another time I have done this in my life was when I was younger.
passages.about: playing a role when younger

passages.quote: My parents had this idea that I needed to be the perfect child and never mess up, so I took this role to the extreme and made them believe that I was as great as they wanted me to be.
passages.about: trying to act like the perfect child

passages.quote: This standard made my life very hard.
passages.about: struggling with perfectionist expectations

passages.quote: I had to get straight A's, or I thought they would be disappointed in me.
passages.about: pressure to get straight A's

passages.quote: I took any time I got a bad grade on a quiz to heart and would think about it over and over again, which caused me to start doing terribly in school.
passages.about: obsessing over bad quiz grades

passages.quote: This role of the perfect child also carried over into sports.
passages.about: acting like a perfect athlete

passages.quote: My family is a huge sports family.
passages.about: family being deeply involved in sports

passages.quote: My older sister was a star softball player, and I felt I had to live up to her shoes.
passages.about: sister being a star softball player

passages.quote: I was practicing 20 to 30 a week to be able to perform this role.
passages.about: practicing sports 20 to 30 hours weekly

passages.quote: This role had terrible effects on my body.
passages.about: experiencing physical harm from sports

passages.quote: I hurt my arm many times and did not tell anyone because I did not want to disappoint my parents.
passages.about: hiding arm injuries from parents

passages.quote: It took me until I turned 15 to realize that my parents only wanted me to be happy, and I was not disappointing them as long as I gave 100 percent effort.
passages.about: realizing parents only wanted happiness

passages.quote: In high school, I hung out with athletes because I was an athlete and had similar views on life.
passages.about: hanging out with fellow athletes

passages.quote: This also links into the roles because I was playing a role in my school as an athlete; thus, I was grouped into this collective consciousness that I was meant to hang out with people like me.
passages.about: being categorized as a high school athlete

passages.quote: This role has worn me down mentally, and I believe that we need to push away from people playing roles.
passages.about: feeling mentally worn down by roles

passages.quote: I am someone who has struggled with self-esteem, and when talking to my peers I have noticed that I am not alone with my feelings.
passages.about: struggling with self-esteem and talking to peers

passages.quote: This feeling of low self-worth has only amplified after coming to college because you're constantly comparing yourself to those you are surrounded by.
passages.about: amplified low self-worth after coming to college

passages.quote: I know that I am not alone when I admit that I have made some unhealthy choices when it comes to low self-esteem.
passages.about: making unhealthy choices due to low self-esteem

passages.quote: I can admit that when I go to the gym, I am not going to be healthy or get stronger; I am going in an attempt to transform my body into one that fits what society calls “desirable”.
passages.about: going to the gym to transform body shape

passages.quote: From the age of three, sports have been a significant part of my life.
passages.about: lifelong involvement in sports

passages.quote: Baseball was, and still is, my favorite sport to play.
passages.about: playing baseball

passages.quote: Ever since I was young, I had some sort of ball in my hand playing around the house.
passages.about: playing with balls as a child

passages.quote: Growing up I have never been the biggest or strongest person that could be used for sports.
passages.about: not being big or strong

passages.quote: Football was always a hardship for me, starting back in middle school.
passages.about: football struggles starting in middle school

passages.quote: He said to a group of us, “Sorry, I will not be able to keep you all on the team because of the size difference.”
passages.about: middle school coach cutting players for size

passages.quote: In high school, I hit a growth spurt, but have never been able to gain as much weight as I needed to, even to this day.
passages.about: struggling to gain weight in high school

passages.quote: He said to me, “When is your body going to get wider?”
passages.about: high school football coach questioning student's body size

passages.quote: I went to a high school where people were favorited in sports due to their last names.
passages.about: nepotism and privilege in high school sports

passages.quote: I did not get many answers, so I started to work out every weekday at school.
passages.about: working out on weekdays at school

passages.quote: Unbelievably, working out was the one solution that helped me get the starting spot, but it only came during my senior year.
passages.about: earning a starting spot senior year

passages.quote: My skills were good enough in baseball to put myself over others.
passages.about: baseball skills

passages.quote: My coaches did not see me as the right fit because I was not big enough to compete with others around me.
passages.about: coaches passing over the student for size

passages.quote: I practiced hard every day, but never got the chance to because hegemonic masculinity confirmed their beliefs that I was not “big enough” to play.
passages.about: practicing hard but being denied starting chances

passages.quote: Even with both genders at our school, we had the upper-class individuals that had the privilege of playing over others.
passages.about: privileged classmates playing over others at school

passages.quote: I work at a gym, here at the University of North Carolina Wilmington, and in my hometown.
passages.about: working at a gym

passages.quote: There, my job is to observe the patrons and make sure no one gets hurt while working out.
passages.about: job duties at the gym

passages.quote: I am also required to spot anyone if they ask for assistance.
passages.about: requirement to spot gym patrons

passages.quote: However, if I am working with another male, men tend to ask them for a sport rather than me because I am a female.
passages.about: men avoiding asking her for a spot

passages.quote: I lift weights every day and am much stronger than most people realize because of my physical appearance.
passages.about: daily weightlifting routine and strength

passages.quote: I am only 5’3 and 135 pounds so men may think I look incapable of spotting them because of my appearance.
passages.about: her height, weight, and perceived capabilities

passages.quote: Not only have I experienced being judged based on my physical appearance while working at the gym, but I have also experienced objectification by men while working out at the gym.
passages.about: experiencing judgment and objectification at the gym

passages.quote: I have had many experiences where I will catch men staring at me or other people will tell me they saw someone creepily staring at me.
passages.about: men staring at her at the gym

passages.quote: I have also had men, some much older, come up and flirt with me.
passages.about: older men flirting with her at gym

passages.quote: Men have followed me around the gym just to stare at me and tried to engage with me in an unwanted way.
passages.about: men following her in the gym

passages.quote: Men have also made unsolicited comments about my body and appearance in the gym.
passages.about: men making unsolicited comments about her body

passages.quote: They have invaded my personal space by standing too close to me or, specifically, one time a man came up behind me while I was squatting and spotted me even though I did not ask for a sport nor did I need one.
passages.about: man giving unsolicited spot while she squatted

passages.quote: I have also witnessed these same exact scenarios happen to other females in the gym.
passages.about: other women facing gym harassment

passages.quote: People often assume that I am physically incapable of certain tasks, such as spotting them in the gym, due to my physical appearance.
passages.about: people doubting her gym capabilities

passages.quote: Men stare at me, follow me, flirt with me, invade my personal space, and make comments about my physical appearance in the gym, which is one example of the effects of the beauty myth.
passages.about: unwanted male attention and harassment in gym

passages.quote: I have personally experienced this in my place of work and while working out.
passages.about: personal experience with differential treatment

passages.quote: Men have made assumptions about my capabilities because of my appearance and common stereotypes created by the beauty myth.
passages.about: men underestimating her physical capabilities

passages.quote: While at work, men tend to ask another male working for a spot rather than me because they assume that women are weak when women can be just as strong as men.
passages.about: men asking male coworkers for spots

passages.quote: Men have also objectified me in the gym by staring, following me, making sexual comments, and unwanted physical contact.
passages.about: objectification and harassment by men at gym

passages.quote: In class, we watched a commercial for GMC.
passages.about: watching a GMC commercial in class

passages.quote: About two years ago, at the end of my junior year of high school, I noticed that I really started paying attention to what I looked like, and what the girls I followed on Instagram looked like.
passages.about: comparing her appearance to girls on Instagram

passages.quote: Since there was nothing else to do but sit at home, I was spending a lot more time on social media than I previously had been.
passages.about: spending more time on social media during COVID-19

passages.quote: After all of this started and a beach trip with my parents was quickly approaching, I decided to start working out a lot.
passages.about: deciding to work out before a beach trip

passages.quote: I played soccer from the time I was 4 years old all the way through high school, and I even ran cross country one year in addition to soccer.
passages.about: playing soccer and running cross country

passages.quote: I began waking up every morning during the week and going for runs in my neighborhood, then doing additional workouts in my garage.
passages.about: running and working out in garage

passages.quote: For the entire summer I ran and did at home workouts hoping to look like the girls I was always comparing myself to.
passages.about: exercising all summer to change body appearance

passages.quote: Today I still run and workout, but my motivation has completely changed.
passages.about: current workout habits and healthier mindset

passages.quote: Although my family always told me I was “skinny”, the beauty myth was telling me that I wasn’t skinny “enough”.
passages.about: family comments versus personal body insecurity

passages.quote: As an individual that has worked since starting high school, it is evident that humans in ourselves are commodities.
passages.about: working since starting high school

passages.quote: Being a minimum wage worker at Duck Donuts, I’ve realized that the value of the product that I produced goes fluctuates throughout the year.
passages.about: working at Duck Donuts for minimum wage

passages.quote: At the beginning of the year business is slow, because of new year resolutions and people are trying to get in shape for summer.
passages.about: slow business at Duck Donuts during New Year

passages.quote: The value of my job changes from month to month because it a mainly labor-induced job.
passages.about: job value changing monthly

passages.quote: What sets myself apart from the theories of Marx and Weber, is that I don’t work for survival in society.
passages.about: not working strictly for survival

passages.quote: As a young woman myself, I can attest to the fact that it’s nice to be taken care of and not have to worry about things in the company of a man.
passages.about: feeling nice to be taken care of by men

passages.quote: Growing up in the Charlotte area, I noticed how people thought my sister and my mother should act and present themselves.
passages.about: noticing expectations placed on mother and sister

passages.quote: For the last few years, she has clearly been aging, as she should be, but rather than people complimenting her for any of her amazing qualities, she gets criticized or joked about for having new wrinkles and/or grey hair.
passages.about: mother criticized and joked about for aging

passages.quote: My father on the other hand gets complimented for looking young, even though my parents are the same age.
passages.about: father complimented for looking young

passages.quote: In school I would always hear my friends and classmates degrade women who were attractive by only referring to them with sexual innuendos rather than for their personality.
passages.about: classmates degrading attractive women with sexual innuendos

passages.quote: Even though many people thought she was a good-looking girl, she was frequently targeted by toxic men who had closed minds.
passages.about: sister targeted by toxic men

passages.quote: If she dyed her hair any color, she was criticized.
passages.about: sister criticized for dyeing her hair

passages.quote: If she gained any weight, she was made fun of.
passages.about: sister mocked for gaining weight

passages.quote: If she liked certain sports, like basketball and golf, she was labelled a tom-boy.
passages.about: sister labelled a tomboy for sports

passages.quote: My sister is very independent and has never relied on her significant other to take care of her, which has made long term relationships hard for her.
passages.about: sister's independence affecting her relationships

passages.quote: While I grew up, I was certainly picked on for not conforming to every gender norm, but since I am a man, much of that discrimination came from other men.
passages.about: student picked on for nonconforming gender norms

passages.quote: I went to middle school and high school with many people who did not conform to the traditional gender roles, so I frequently saw them targeted by (mostly) men who expected them to look a certain type of way.
passages.about: nonconforming peers targeted by men

passages.quote: For example, my friend Thalia in middle school always dressed very neutral and would wear clothes that were not particularly women’s style, and she was criticized.
passages.about: friend Thalia criticized for dressing neutrally

passages.quote: If she had to dress up for a presentation, she would wear nice clothes, but would never wear a dress and heels.
passages.about: Thalia avoiding dresses and heels for presentations

passages.quote: Fast forward to Thalia in late high school and she was thought of as an icon for her style, because she did try to look presentable and trendy, she just did not conform to traditional women’s attire.
passages.about: Thalia admired as a high school style icon

passages.quote: Being a Male Asian-American that can afford college and has the resources to be successful shows an incredible amount of predisposed privilege.
passages.about: student's background and college resources

passages.quote: I have come to recognize this privilege and have realized that social standing is in direct correlation with how society sees you.
passages.about: student recognizing their own privilege

passages.quote: One Question I repeatedly hear from my roommate is, “Why are you always so hard on yourself?”
passages.about: roommate asking why the student is hard on herself

passages.quote: For example, I complain about my grades if they are less than an A, as well as if I make a perfectly normal mistake.
passages.about: complaining about grades less than an A

passages.quote: When I was growing up, I noticed that in every friend group, I played the role of the “dumb” one, frequently being teased for my awkward jokes or irrelevant comments.
passages.about: being teased by friends while growing up

passages.quote: This trend additionally followed me into middle school as well as high school within the friend groups I would weave through.
passages.about: being the teased friend in middle and high school

passages.quote: If I am performing the role of daughter, I am expected to be responsible, independent, and live up to the expectations of my older sister.
passages.about: family expectations to match older sister

passages.quote: Being all these things and not slipping up is very difficult and trust me, I have fallen out of character many of times before.
passages.about: failing to meet family expectations

passages.quote: When I was in my senior year of high school I had an open spot in my schedule, I did not have to take a math class which I was incredibly happy about but then I was tasked with the decision of filling a spot I wished I could have just left empty.
passages.about: choosing high school schedule classes

passages.quote: I was dreading choosing a class until I came upon a weight training class, I was ecstatic!
passages.about: deciding to take weight training

passages.quote: I had been working out for a while at that point but I did not belong to a gym and did not own any home weights and I liked the idea of getting my work out over with during school hours so I wouldn't have to worry about it when I got home when I was already worried about getting homework done and spending time with my friends and other chores I had to get done around the house.
passages.about: student's workout routine and motivation

passages.quote: I knew I was not going to go in there and lift super heavy, but I was a little disappointed that to start with I could only lift the bar.
passages.about: lifting only the bar initially

passages.quote: I could often hear other classmates laughing at me as I did my sets and making jokes about it being pointless for me to even try and some of the guys would say I was taking up their time to lift.
passages.about: classmates mocking the student lifting weights

passages.quote: I was the only girl in the class.
passages.about: being the only female student

passages.quote: I told them I was a beginner, and I knew I could not lift much weight, but I told them that I truly wanted to improve and get stronger and more muscular and that I did not take the class to joke around, waste their time or take up their workout time, I truly wanted to become good at weight lifting.
passages.about: explaining her goals to male classmates

passages.quote: Nobody seemed to care that I had good intentions.
passages.about: classmates ignoring her good intentions

passages.quote: I am considered to be quite petite so I was judged even before they saw I could only lift the bar.
passages.about: being judged for her petite size

passages.quote: We were all paired as two-person partner groups.
passages.about: pairing up in weight class

passages.quote: My partner seemed very upset to be paired with me and he would talk to the other guys in class but then when it was time for us to lift weights together he would put in his AirPods and refuse to talk to me and was very reluctant to take out his earbuds when I was waving at him to get his attention which I rarely did only if needed.
passages.about: partner ignoring the student during class

passages.quote: One day in class I was lifting the bar for a bench press when he spotted me and I was struggling, it was obvious I needed his help lifting the bar back onto the rack, I said: “I cannot get it, can you help?” He looked me straight in the eyes and saw me struggling and refused to help me lift it onto the rack, I dropped it on my chest, and it rolled down my ribcage onto my stomach.
passages.about: partner refusing to spot bench press

passages.quote: I always felt like an outsider in that class, it was although they all had a supportive and healthily competitive community, and I was the “other.”
passages.about: feeling like an outsider in class

passages.quote: Around this time, I started seeing videos of female weightlifters on social media, I was envious of their bodies, and it made me feel even worse that I could not lift anywhere close to what they could.
passages.about: watching weightlifters on social media

passages.quote: It very negatively affected my self-esteem and my relationship with food and my body image.
passages.about: negative effects on self-esteem and body image

passages.quote: The weight training class I took was certainly a hegemonic masculinity environment and, in my situation, it was damaging.
passages.about: taking the damaging weight training class

passages.quote: The most obvious way I was blatantly put into the category as other and was made to feel as though I did not belong was one day, we had a substitute in class, he looked me up and down and his face twisted with annoyance and disgust, and he asked me “ do you even lift anything in here?” I felt truly angry and isolated.
passages.about: substitute teacher insulting the student

passages.quote: I kept getting the same message that I was the other and I was in everyone else's way.
passages.about: feeling like she was in the way

passages.quote: The message that I was weak, and incomplete was repetitively sent to me in different ways.
passages.about: receiving messages of being weak

passages.quote: The boys in my class and the substitute teacher supported treating women as other and a hegemonic masculine environment.
passages.about: treatment by boys and substitute teacher

passages.quote: I experienced this treatment firsthand in the weight training class I took.
passages.about: experiencing exclusion in weight training class

passages.quote: The way my other classmates treated me and the way the substitute teacher spoke to me supported a hegemonic masculinity environment where I was made to feel like I did not belong, and I was made to feel like I was weak, not capable of improvement.
passages.about: feeling excluded by classmates and substitute

passages.quote: I lift weights with my husband, and I also occasionally lift weights with one of our male mutual friends and neither of them judge me and they are both incredibly supportive during our workouts, so I know it is possible for men to not be toxic towards women in the gym.
passages.about: lifting weights with husband and friend

passages.quote: I was born in Lebanon and moved to the United States when I was four years old, and thus I had the experience of trying to acclimate to a change in culture coupled with the attempt to make friends and fit in at school.
passages.about: moving from Lebanon to the US as a child

passages.quote: For instance, I would get uncomfortable when waiters at restaurants could not understand what my parents said due to their accent.
passages.about: waiters having trouble understanding parents' accents

passages.quote: Furthermore, I would wince when thinking of people struggling to pronounce my last name at awards ceremonies and when teachers would ask me to pronounce my last name.
passages.about: people struggling to pronounce student's last name

passages.quote: In order to make the trip worthwhile over Christmas break, I would skip a few days of class and as such would be asked to make an educational presentation on my trip to Lebanon to share with the class when I returned.
passages.about: giving school presentations about trips to Lebanon

passages.quote: After the tenth grade, I went to the North Carolina School of Science and Mathematics (NCSSM), which had a far greater level of diversity and which had several multicultural events occurring throughout my time there.
passages.about: attending high school at NCSSM

passages.quote: Moreover, I have been mistaken for a Hispanic person on multiple occasions by Hispanics.
passages.about: being mistaken for Hispanic

passages.quote: In the summer, I would be saddened by the fact that my skin would get darker, pushing me further away from the race I wanted to be.
passages.about: feeling sad about skin getting darker in summer

passages.quote: When growing up, I had friends, the majority of whom were white; this was due to the fact that my school was predominantly white and that I held stereotypes about the black students, which led me to avoid attempting to start friendships with them.
passages.about: growing up with mostly white friends

passages.quote: At UNCW, I have been fortunate enough to join multicultural clubs and to meet people who have immigrated to the U.S like I did.
passages.about: joining multicultural clubs at UNCW

passages.quote: At NCSSM, I went to several multicultural events, allowing me to learn more about the cultures of which my peers were a part and to have fun doing so by eating food, listening to music, and playing games which came from those cultures.
passages.about: attending multicultural events at NCSSM

passages.quote: Comparing NCSSM to my previous high school, Gray’s Creek High School (GCHS), I can see stark differences in the amount of pressure I felt to place myself within a racial hierarchy.
passages.about: comparing experiences at GCHS and NCSSM

passages.quote: A prime example is this past weekend, I was at the local Chipotle in Wilmington and as I ate my delicious burrito, I noticed an older teen was watching a YouTube vide while eating dinner with his mother.
passages.about: observing a teen on YouTube at Chipotle

passages.quote: The experience looked awkward as the mother was trying to make conversation, which can be explained by Erving Goffman and Yuval Harari.
passages.about: watching an awkward mother-son interaction

passages.quote: I attended these camps for four years and was exposed to a culture that I would have never found if I had not attended the camps.
passages.about: attending Turtle Island camp for four years

passages.quote: During my four summers attending the camp, I never saw a single camper or counselor that wasn’t white.
passages.about: observing only white campers and counselors at camp

passages.quote: So while there were women living on the land during the boys two week camp, our exposure to them was limited as much as possible.
passages.about: having limited exposure to women during summer camp

passages.quote: Nobody was ever seriously hurt but there were at least one or two fights per summer between campers.
passages.about: witnessing fights between campers each summer

passages.quote: I specifically remember a game called gladiator that we were playing during my second year.
passages.about: playing the gladiator log game second year

passages.quote: It was an activity in which our counselor would march the group about a mile into the woods in a random direction and make the campers wait until the sun went down.
passages.about: being marched into the woods for night hikes

passages.quote: The counselor would then confiscate any flashlights the campers had brought with them and would make the campers navigate their way back to the camp by themselves with no light.
passages.about: having flashlights confiscated during the night hike challenge

passages.quote: So while we were learning traditional survival skills, the camp was also reinforcing this idea of independence and a toughness-over-all mentality.
passages.about: learning traditional survival skills at camp

passages.quote: Looking back on it now, I feel lucky to have mostly avoided the ridicule of my cabinmates.
passages.about: mostly avoiding ridicule from cabinmates

passages.quote: And I feel real remorse for not standing up for people who were being bullied.
passages.about: regretting not standing up for bullied peers

passages.quote: In tv entertainment I get caught up in an actors life so much that when I see them in different program it catches me off guard.
passages.about: getting caught up in actors' roles across TV programs

passages.quote: For the longest time whenever I saw Mr. Krasinski in any film, I always gave him the persona as Jim from the office.
passages.about: always viewing John Krasinski as Jim Halpert

passages.quote: In class, we talked about the start of religion and what led to the expansion.
passages.about: discussing religious origins in sociology class

passages.quote: This is the exact reaction I have seen time and time again when a male walks in the room from a suggested sexual encounter.
passages.about: seeing men celebrated after suggested sexual encounters

passages.quote: I recently walked into a room with a guy, whom we will refer to as Kevin, from a late dinner on campus, but the image of us walking in together created a different idea.
passages.about: walking into a room with a male friend

passages.quote: All of Kevin’s friends, particularly his roommate, were extremely excited.
passages.about: friends celebrating Kevin entering the room

passages.quote: Watching this unfold, my face reddened from embarrassment, even though I knew that nothing had happened.
passages.about: feeling embarrassed by peers' assumptions

passages.quote: Throughout the entire night, every time Kevin made his way to specifically talk to me, or touch me on the arm, or make any sort of “move”, cheers from the other men began.
passages.about: peers cheering whenever Kevin approached her

passages.quote: However, not a single girl spoke to me the rest of the night.
passages.about: being ostracized by girls all night

passages.quote: This is one of many, many similar experiences I have encountered in my relatively short lifespan.
passages.about: encountering similar experiences throughout life

passages.quote: Just a few nights ago, a girl, whom we will refer to as Carla, sent a photo of her and a guy to my dorm’s group chat.
passages.about: Carla sending a photo to dorm group chat

passages.quote: I was in the room with most of the people in the group chat, and the guys were shocked, impressed, yet also disgusted with her behavior.
passages.about: witnessing peers gossip and judge Carla

passages.quote: My roommate reached out to her and told her what was being discussed.
passages.about: roommate telling Carla about the dorm's gossip

passages.quote: She responded, explaining that she hadn’t even kissed the guy.
passages.about: Carla explaining nothing sexual happened

passages.quote: For high school, I went to a private boarding school where the boys were in the military and the ladies were in leadership.
passages.about: attending a private boarding school for high school

passages.quote: I am more passionate about the topic of why hegemonic masculinity is wrong and negatively effects guys now that I've witnessed it myself.
passages.about: witnessing the negative effects of hegemonic masculinity

passages.quote: When boys first arrive at Culver, they go through a process known as "new cadet," in which they must clean and memorize "common knowledge" about the school in order to pass boards at the end.
passages.about: boys undergoing new cadet initiation at boarding school

passages.quote: Whenever you go to Culver, you see the bright young males go in on orientation day and almost completely transform into a new person.
passages.about: observing male students transform at boarding school

passages.quote: Growing up as a woman, I have viewed life much different than a man would.
passages.about: growing up viewing life as a woman

passages.quote: My family has not experienced this, but I recently watched a movie The Interns that speaks to this situation.
passages.about: student's family dynamic not having stay-at-home dad

passages.quote: For me this time was right before I started middle school, the happy meals no longer filled me up like they once did and I had started to get to big for the play place.
passages.about: outgrowing Happy Meals and McDonald's play places

passages.quote: I have played soccer throughout my entire life, beginning when I was around 5 years old.
passages.about: playing soccer since childhood

passages.quote: I have continued on to play soccer in middle school, high school, and still today while in college.
passages.about: playing soccer through school and college

passages.quote: Along the way, I have made many Hispanic friends who are deeply engaged in the culture of the sport.
passages.about: making Hispanic friends through soccer

passages.quote: Many of my current friends are Hispanic and frequently invite me to cultural gatherings and family events.
passages.about: friends inviting the student to family events

passages.quote: I even currently play on an adult league soccer team that is exclusively Hispanic aside from myself.
passages.about: playing on an adult Hispanic soccer team

passages.quote: This team, made up of many of my best friends, plays and practices together every week and often go out for dinner together.
passages.about: practicing and having dinner with teammates

passages.quote: One of my many experiences with this team came several months ago when we had an open practice that anyone could attend.
passages.about: attending an open soccer practice

passages.quote: As usual I arrived early with one of my best friends, Adrian, and a few others on the team.
passages.about: arriving early to practice with Adrian

passages.quote: When we arrived at the park, the field we normally practice on was taken up by a large group playing flag football.
passages.about: finding the practice field occupied

passages.quote: The rest of the team and I all waited by our cars as more and more people showed up for our upcoming practice.
passages.about: waiting by cars for practice

passages.quote: These people playing football were primarily black and the Hispanic individuals started using racial slurs amongst each other and making many racist comments.
passages.about: Hispanic teammates using racial slurs

passages.quote: During one game in particular, we played against a primarily Columbian team who were made up of individuals of a different heritage and slightly different complexion.
passages.about: playing against a Colombian soccer team

passages.quote: After the game, several slurs were used between players of my team and the Columbians.
passages.about: players exchanging slurs after a game

passages.quote: When discussing the “Doing Gender” reading by West and Zimmerman in class, we came up with a list of traits that society associates with a specific gender.
passages.about: listing gender traits in a class discussion

passages.quote: I would scroll for hours on end on TikTok, watching girls compare themselves to celebrities, influencers, models – any woman who they believed to be perfect; any woman they deemed a Heather.
passages.about: scrolling TikTok watching comparison videos during quarantine

passages.quote: After watching so many of these videos, I began to feel the same way: How could anyone ever think I’m beautiful, when there are women who look like that?!
passages.about: feeling insecure after watching TikTok videos

passages.quote: I continued to watch the videos, and after some time, I noticed something.
passages.about: noticing that original video posters were also insecure

passages.quote: I believed that I got cheated on because I wasn’t pretty enough for him.
passages.about: believing an ex cheated due to her appearance

passages.quote: When I was 16 years old, I got my first job at a local Panera Bread.
passages.about: getting first job at Panera Bread at sixteen

passages.quote: I was quickly trained and became one of the most dependable employees they had.
passages.about: becoming a dependable employee at Panera

passages.quote: I was the first one they always called to cover shifts, train people, and handle mishaps at the cash register.
passages.about: being called to cover shifts and train staff

passages.quote: All the while I was working there, I was paid $9 an hour.
passages.about: earning nine dollars an hour at Panera

passages.quote: I was training boys my age who were making more than I was.
passages.about: training male peers who were paid more

passages.quote: When I brought this up to management, they denied that there was a gap in my pay with the boys I was training.
passages.about: management denying wage gap with trainee boys

passages.quote: Management tended to hire a lot of “pretty” people, but these people were not good at their job.
passages.about: management hiring attractive people who worked poorly

passages.quote: After all of my hard work, some of the managers started to realize, after a year, that I was a good employee to have around.
passages.about: managers recognizing student was a good worker

passages.quote: They started to promise me a promotion and raise, but that never did happen.
passages.about: unfulfilled promises of promotion and raise

passages.quote: In my attempt to try and resolve the problems that existed at Panera, I spoke with managers on multiple occasions about the promotion, promises of a raise, and harassment from a male co-worker with nothing to be changed.
passages.about: reporting pay issues and harassment with no resolution

passages.quote: Management would oftentimes try to get more of the male employees to higher ranks or work in the kitchen as line cooks whereas female employees would be recruited to work in the bakery or as a cashier.
passages.about: gender-segregated job roles observed at Panera Bread

passages.quote: In my own personal experience, I had overheard constant discussions and a noticeable obsession with "fraternities and frat parties" when I arrived at UNCW for my first year.
passages.about: hearing constant talk about frat parties at UNCW

passages.quote: So, when I attended to my first frat party with my new college mates, it commenced right away.
passages.about: attending their first college frat party

passages.quote: After dollishly getting ready for hours to impress a group of strangers we had never met, my friends and I ordered an Uber.
passages.about: getting ready and taking an Uber with friends

passages.quote: When we arrived, there were five older college boys in front of the house, seated on filthy lawn chairs.
passages.about: arriving at a frat house guarded by boys

passages.quote: All five of them stood up as we approached in a group of four.
passages.about: approaching the fraternity house entrance

passages.quote: They assessed our "beauty" by looking at all of us up and down, then turned around and talked for a few seconds.
passages.about: being scrutinized by fraternity boys outside the party

passages.quote: My friends and I stood there, uneasy but curiously anxiously anticipating these boys' approval.
passages.about: waiting uneasily for frat boys' approval

passages.quote: One of the boys asked for my friend's phone number and asked if she wanted a drink, but she refused, and the boy gave her an odd and disturbed expression.
passages.about: friend refusing a drink and phone number request

passages.quote: With an irritated tone, he welcomed everyone except her to the event.
passages.about: frat boy excluding the student's friend

passages.quote: We certainly couldn't go without her, so we left the party.
passages.about: leaving the frat party together

passages.quote: "Don't ever come back," one of the boys said as we walked away.
passages.about: being told never to return by frat boy

passages.quote: Of course, I'd been to a lot of other parties like this, and when I stepped inside, I saw a lot of girls standing around waiting for men's approval to have a nice time.
passages.about: seeing girls seek male approval at other parties

passages.quote: In a similar situation, one of my best friends at UNCW who is gay asked if he could join us for a frat party one night.
passages.about: gay friend asking to attend a frat party

passages.quote: When 7 of my friends and I arrived, including my gay friend, we approached the boys, and a similar, but even more heated situation ensued.
passages.about: arriving at a frat party with gay friend

passages.quote: The boys rose up and looked about, wondering, "What is this?" referring to my friend, who was dressed in girl shorts and a cropped t-shirt.
passages.about: frat boys questioning the gay friend's appearance

passages.quote: As we began to walk in, some of the boys began to come at us, forcing my friend away.
passages.about: frat boys aggressively pushing the friend away

passages.quote: He informed us that individuals like him are not allowed to attend these events.
passages.about: being told gay people cannot attend

passages.quote: We asked several questions and tried to come up with a solution.
passages.about: questioning the fraternity boys' refusal

passages.quote: People like him, the boys continued, pull the females away from the very premise of the gathering.
passages.about: frat boys explaining why gay friend was excluded

passages.quote: We were also thrown out of this fraternity as a result of this.
passages.about: getting thrown out of the fraternity party

passages.quote: I am a lifeguard at a pool, and I have been told that I look weak, so people often assume that I am not very good at my job.
passages.about: assumptions about being weak at work

passages.quote: She even had me teach the new lifeguards how to vacuum at the beginning of last summer.
passages.about: teaching new lifeguards how to vacuum

passages.quote: We have to carry stacks of chairs across the pool deck every Thursday, so he used to get upset when only girls were scheduled for that shift, saying things such as, “I wish the guys were here” or “We would have had this done in 10 minutes if there were no girls working”.
passages.about: manager complaining about female staff carrying chairs

passages.quote: One day when I was working, Marco asked me to finish vacuuming the pool.
passages.about: manager asking student to vacuum pool

passages.quote: He said that Marco told him to come help me take out the vacuum because he did not think that I could do it myself.
passages.about: coworker sent to help with pool vacuum

passages.quote: Later, my friend told me that our manager was making jokes about me to the other guards and saying that I was probably too dumb to understand them.
passages.about: manager insulting student's intellect to coworkers

passages.quote: Every time that Marco asked me to sweep under the pavilion, he would come with me and watch me to make sure I was doing it right.
passages.about: manager micromanaging student while sweeping

passages.quote: He would even take the broom and dustpan out of my hands and show me what he thought was the ‘right’ way to sweep.
passages.about: manager taking sweeping tools to demonstrate

passages.quote: Another girl that I work with tried to defend my abilities to Marco, but she took it too far and ended up calling him a “cunt”.
passages.about: coworker cursing at manager while defending student

passages.quote: Knowing this, he used it to his advantage and threatened to get my friend fired.
passages.about: manager threatening to fire student's friend

passages.quote: In an attempt to resolve our problems with Marco, my friends and I talked to the other manager, Megan, one day about how he was making us feel.
passages.about: reporting manager's behavior to another manager

passages.quote: She told us that our descriptions do not fit into her experiences with him and that we should not let what he says get in our heads.
passages.about: manager dismissing student's workplace complaint

passages.quote: Since she was offered the position as manager, no one on the board has shown her any respect, and they do not think that she is competent enough to run the pool without help.
passages.about: board disrespecting female manager's competence

passages.quote: I often feel like I play into the stereotypes that go along with the beauty myth because my physical appearance is consistent with the conventional beauty standard in America.
passages.about: feeling perceived through conventional beauty standards

passages.quote: Although she is the manager and Marco is the assistant manager, the board members tell Marco important information about the pool instead of her.
passages.about: board bypassing female manager for male assistant

passages.quote: My first semester here I was deciding if I wanted to play club volleyball here at UNCW because volleyball has always been something that I love playing and I thought that it would be very good for me and even a way to make some friends.
passages.about: deciding whether to join club volleyball at UNCW

passages.quote: The first day that I went it everyone was just playing king of the court and pick up games and it was really fun.
passages.about: attending the first day of club volleyball

passages.quote: About 30 minutes into playing the boys club volleyball team showed up and wanted to play pick up with us.
passages.about: boys club team arriving to play pickup

passages.quote: I did not think anything of it and thought “oh this is going to be fun because I bet they are good”.
passages.about: thinking playing pickup with the boys would be fun

passages.quote: Whenever the boys team came up to us they started acting kind of weird and I did not think anything of it just because I thought oh well maybe they don’t really know who we are yet.
passages.about: boys acting weird upon approaching them

passages.quote: They ended up sitting on the sidelines and just watching us play.
passages.about: boys sitting and watching them play first

passages.quote: Shortly after they came back up to us and were like can we play with you guys and make teams.
passages.about: boys asking to make teams and play

passages.quote: Of course we said yes and none of us thought anything about it until about 20 minutes into playing one of the boys came up to me and said “I didn’t expect you to be that good at volleyball”.
passages.about: boy remarking he didn't expect student to be good

passages.quote: I was really confused because I had no idea who he was and thought to myself well did he expect me to be bad or not know how to play.
passages.about: feeling confused by the boy's remark

passages.quote: I kept playing with them and they were constantly complimenting me and saying things like wow you are really good for your height.
passages.about: receiving backhanded compliments while playing

passages.quote: I know that they did not think anything about that but to me it felt like a backhanded compliment because they were straight up telling me that they didn’t think I was going to be good and I know it was just because I was a girl.
passages.about: feeling backhanded compliments were due to being a girl

passages.quote: Eventually, I put two and two together and realized that they just expected me to not be as good or be able to keep up and actually play a good game with them just because I was a girl.
passages.about: realizing boys underestimated her volleyball skills

passages.quote: I know that mens volleyball is a lot different than women at the professional level but anything other than that girls can usually keep up with a boys team or at least everytime I have played a boys team I have been able to.
passages.about: past experience keeping up when playing boys' teams

passages.quote: That honestly bothered me so much just because the boys came in and just assumed that we were not going to be good I guess and looked at us as inferior to them just because we were girls.
passages.about: feeling bothered by the boys' assumptions

passages.quote: We have talked about gender in society a lot in class and also about different scientists who talk about it and have theories.
passages.about: discussing gender theories in sociology class

passages.quote: We read “The Yellow Wallpaper” by Charlotte Perkins Gilman, which is a story based on the nineteenth centuy, for questions in class and that article really stood out to me just for the sole fact that the wife in this story was just looked at as women and not even a person just because of her gender and her husband sees himself as more powerful than her.
passages.about: reading The Yellow Wallpaper for class questions

passages.quote: We also read “ Women as Other” by Simone de Beauvoir which has the same concept about women being treated differently than men.
passages.about: reading Simone de Beauvoir in class

passages.quote: I have personally experienced this in college and definitely have many more times than that.
passages.about: experiencing gender-based assumptions in college

passages.quote: I have worked at my school’s after school program for four years throughout highschool.
passages.about: working at school's after school program during high school

passages.quote: Most of my tasks once I clock in after the final school bell rings include helping children with homework and communicating with parents over the phone or in person while simultaneously making sure children aren’t shoving each other down while they play.
passages.about: job duties at the after school program

passages.quote: Because of my many years of experience, I was able to participate in training new workers, and having some input on new applicants to the program.
passages.about: training new workers and giving input on applicants

passages.quote: Although I have worked with this program longer than any of my other coworkers, I am getting paid $1.20 less than some of my fellow coworkers.
passages.about: earning less pay than coworkers despite longer tenure

passages.quote: After conversing with the only other female that works alongside me, we realized that the two of us were being paid the exact same amount, while our male coworkers were receiving $1.20 higher.
passages.about: learning male coworkers were paid more than female coworkers

passages.quote: I approached my female boss after work, asking to speak with her in private with the hope that I could resolve this issue occurring at my workplace.
passages.about: confronting boss privately about unequal pay

passages.quote: However, to my astonishment, the conversation was shut down immediately when I expressed that I was inquiring about unequal pay.
passages.about: boss shutting down conversation about unequal pay

passages.quote: I was not even given the opportunity to express my thoughts on the matter, and was told to not discuss my pay with my coworkers again.
passages.about: boss forbidding discussion of pay with coworkers

passages.quote: Afterwards, I felt defeated.
passages.about: feeling defeated after meeting with boss

passages.quote: I expressed what was happening to my entire class, and my male teacher, who was enraged by the fact I was getting paid less.
passages.about: telling history class and teacher about the pay gap

passages.quote: My other coworker who was also getting paid less was in this class, and she told her side of the story to him as well.
passages.about: coworker telling teacher about pay inequality

passages.quote: After talking with us in private after class, he told us he was going to the principal to discuss this matter because she overlooked the summer camp and after school program.
passages.about: teacher offering to report unequal pay to principal

passages.quote: A few weeks go by, and my boss approaches my friend and I, asking to talk after work.
passages.about: boss requesting a meeting after work with employees

passages.quote: The only thing my boss was able to offer us is that she would talk with our administrator, and see what she could do about getting our issue resolved.
passages.about: boss promising to speak with an administrator

passages.quote: After this past summer, I quit working at the summer camp.
passages.about: quitting job at the summer camp

passages.quote: When I turned in my two weeks notice, I informed my boss I was quitting due to my rights not being fulfilled at this workplace.
passages.about: telling boss reason for resigning

passages.quote: I find that even I do it when talking about an injury because, often, a man in the conversation will counter the pain with the question of “But have you even had this happen to you?” or something similar.
passages.about: downplaying injury pain around men

passages.quote: My family pushed classic feminine and masculine traits on my siblings and I.
passages.about: Family pushing gender roles on student and siblings

passages.quote: My mother didn’t go to college and she met my father at a job.
passages.about: Mother meeting father at a job

passages.quote: After they got married and had my brother, Jack, my mother was deemed the one to stay home and raise Jack while my father worked.
passages.about: Mother staying home to raise brother Jack

passages.quote: My mother didn’t have much say during political discourse over dinner; how women should live their lives, what is a respectable woman, how men should be the ‘man of the house,’ etc.
passages.about: Mother staying silent during family dinner discussions

passages.quote: My neighbor that I had playdates with, Cecelia, decided to stop hanging out with me because I was too boyish.
passages.about: Neighbor ending friendship over student being boyish

passages.quote: I played soccer for the majority of my life and she thought that I should be partaking in girlier sports like cheerleading.
passages.about: Playing soccer instead of cheerleading

passages.quote: That said, I moderated my life to still play soccer and look the way that I did, but I acted more feminine; more flirty, paying my attention to boys and if they liked me or not.
passages.about: Acting more feminine in elementary school

passages.quote: In middle school, I started becoming a woman; I got my period, I developed breasts, I was taller than some of the boys, the whole shabang.
passages.about: Student physically maturing in middle school

passages.quote: I was told to wear more than our uniform required.
passages.about: Told to cover up beyond the school uniform

passages.quote: I was the hot topic of seventh and eighth grade due to my breasts.
passages.about: Being discussed in middle school for body development

passages.quote: I have seen him cry once in all my life, he usually releases his emotions through anger.
passages.about: Father crying only once in life

passages.quote: The other girls in my class started to spread rumors about me in attempts to make the boys stop liking me.
passages.about: Girls spreading rumors about the student

passages.quote: Personally the domino effect didn’t end for me until my junior year of high school.
passages.about: End of pleasing standards in high school junior year

passages.quote: Because of the personality change I had in fifth grade, that carried on in middle school.
passages.about: Fifth grade personality change continuing to middle school

passages.quote: An example of this is Christianity, from my personal experience in church, the bible says that God will love you no matter what.
passages.about: student's personal experience attending church

passages.quote: I have lived my entire life as a substantially underweight human being, I have been picked on harshly about my “scrawniness” by friends, family members and even complete strangers.
passages.about: being mocked for being underweight

passages.quote: Many of my friends in grade school only weighed maybe 20 to 30 pounds more than me, yet I was always singled out regarding my weight.
passages.about: being singled out regarding weight in grade school

passages.quote: Grownups, people I was supposed to look up to and respect, poked fun at me about my body and I could never make sense of it.
passages.about: grownups poking fun at the student's body

passages.quote: This has been something that I have constantly dealt with and when I told my parents the topic of this paper, they themselves were taken by surprise at how true the double standard truly is.
passages.about: discussing this paper's topic with parents

passages.quote: They had gone my whole life never knowing the issues that I had with constantly being criticized by others regarding my weight.
passages.about: parents being unaware of student's struggles

passages.quote: My girlfriend is the first person to ever explain, using this reason, as to why people believe it is okay to skinny shame.
passages.about: girlfriend explaining reasons behind skinny shaming

passages.quote: I have proved people wrong within these categories a vast number of times, but there have also been times where I let myself down and was even further ridiculed.
passages.about: being ridiculed when failing to prove others wrong

passages.quote: Growing up, and even still today, I have always been a more introverted person.
passages.about: being an introverted person

passages.quote: However, as I have started to get older, and especially towards the end of high school, I noticed that I was becoming more confident and was shifting into a more outgoing person.
passages.about: becoming more confident in late high school

passages.quote: I have been playing softball since I was around 8 years old.
passages.about: playing softball since age eight

passages.quote: From growing up playing tee ball in the yard, to playing in my first travel game, to playing on the varsity team in high school, a significant portion of my life has been devoted to softball.
passages.about: playing softball throughout childhood and high school

passages.quote: It was a shock, then, when I realized that high school softball was actually the hardest setting to act like myself in.
passages.about: struggling to be herself in high school softball

passages.quote: In my town, softball was completely run by politics.
passages.about: politics in hometown softball

passages.quote: From the very first day of tryouts freshman year, I could tell that I was not one of the popular girls.
passages.about: freshman year softball tryouts

passages.quote: The coach loved the girls in one friend group who were showing off and acting like they owned the place.
passages.about: coach favoring specific girls at tryouts

passages.quote: At that point in time, I was completely terrified to be playing with the upperclassmen and felt like I shouldn’t be there at all.
passages.about: feeling terrified playing with upperclassmen

passages.quote: Even as the years passed, I noticed I was still stuck as the shy underclassmen.
passages.about: remaining cast as shy in softball

passages.quote: At school before practice, I was able to be myself, but the second I arrived to practice it was like a switch flipped and I was back to my quiet, freshman self.
passages.about: acting quiet upon arriving at softball practice

passages.quote: I didn’t realize this was happening for a long time, but by senior year I really began to notice that I was a completely different person around my teammates than while I was with my other friends.
passages.about: noticing personality change around teammates senior year

passages.quote: When I was at softball, I had tried a few times to change my role and become the outgoing person I was outside of practice.
passages.about: trying to change persona at softball practice

passages.quote: I remember the first time I stepped foot in the cafeteria at my high school.
passages.about: first time entering the high school cafeteria

passages.quote: There were about three hundred or so students there, and they were all grouped off.
passages.about: seeing students grouped off in cafeteria

passages.quote: I noticed that there was not much integration; the black people were sitting with other black people, Latinos were sitting with other Latinos, and the white people were sitting with other white people.
passages.about: observing racial segregation in cafeteria

passages.quote: If you look closely, most of the time the cafeteria will be split into about three or four groups, but there will be a few outliers (like myself) who will sit with any group.
passages.about: sitting with any cafeteria group

passages.quote: Growing up, I’ve witnessed and experienced the pitfalls of the class system firsthand.
passages.about: experiencing the class system firsthand

passages.quote: I was raised in a family that would probably be most closely defined as lower middle class, and both of my parents worked very hard.
passages.about: growing up in a lower middle class family

passages.quote: My dad worked as a mechanic doing serious physical labor every day, and my mom worked late hours as a nurse.
passages.about: parents working physically demanding and late jobs

passages.quote: Despite all their hard work, this was still only enough to provide the necessities to our family, which I’m very grateful for.
passages.about: family only earning enough for necessities

passages.quote: I have had to take out loans for college and I hope to pay them off as soon as I can after graduation.
passages.about: taking out student loans for college

passages.quote: Witnessing my mom come home on weekends past 2 am and dad clearly exhausted after every shift left a strong impression on me.
passages.about: parents coming home late and exhausted from work

passages.quote: Many of the families in my community struggled to make ends meet, and as a kid we were never able to splurge on lavish vacations or cars like our fellow classmates.
passages.about: family unable to afford vacations or nice cars

passages.quote: I have worked many small part-time jobs, ice cream scooper, server, babysitter, volleyball coach, feed shop warehouse worker, farm hand, and most recently a metal worker for a golf company.
passages.about: listing various past part-time jobs

passages.quote: I was sixteen at the time and had applied for a part time job at a local feed store as a warehouse hand.
passages.about: applying for a feed store warehouse job

passages.quote: I was raised on Black Angus Family Farm, so I am used to labor intensive jobs, and throwing feed bags and hay bales.
passages.about: growing up on a family farm

passages.quote: Upon turning my application into the owner of the feed store who was a middle-aged man, he quickly questioned me and asked me if I meant to apply for the warehouse position.
passages.about: store owner questioning applicant's chosen position

passages.quote: I told him yes, that I was a farm hand, and I would prefer that to be opposed to being behind a counter all day.
passages.about: expressing preference for warehouse physical labor

passages.quote: He in turn asked me if I could lift a feed bag; I demonstrated by lifting a 75-pound bag of grass seed.
passages.about: lifting a heavy grass seed bag

passages.quote: The owner simply just smiled at me and said I would look better behind the counter and unless I worked the counter, he would not offer me a job because the warehouse is for men, and it would not be right to have a “little girl” back there.
passages.about: owner denying warehouse job due to gender

passages.quote: I faced a similar challenge when I worked in the metals department of a golf company where I was the only female among male colleagues.
passages.about: working as only female in metals department

passages.quote: During my interview, they asked if I was okay with getting my hands dirty and emphasized that the job required physical labor.
passages.about: interview questions about physical labor

passages.quote: Despite this, I was hired.
passages.about: getting hired at golf company

passages.quote: For instance, while washing a metal pan, a colleague told me to stay in the kitchen because that is where I belonged, and to come in only when the real work was done, so I could clean up the mess, and that I look too good to be doing dirty work.
passages.about: colleague making sexist remarks while washing pan

passages.quote: Recently, we had a project with 650 metal ball markers, I completed three in the time it took my male colleagues to finish one.
passages.about: outperforming male colleagues on ball markers project

passages.quote: They make jokes about needing to give me directions on where to drop off shipments, even asking if they needed to draw me a map, because they know women are dictionally challenged.
passages.about: colleagues joking about giving directions

passages.quote: I am even reminded of how to do basic tasks I perform every day by my supervisor.
passages.about: supervisor repeatedly reminding how to do tasks

passages.quote: In my first puzzle the feed store owner assumed that I could not handle the physical demands of the job simply because of my gender, and even denied me of the job because I am woman.
passages.about: feed store owner denying job over gender

passages.quote: In my second puzzle, my male colleagues at the golf company treated me the only female employee differently, making sexist comments and belittling my abilities, even when I proved that I was capable and efficient in my work.
passages.about: golf company colleagues making sexist comments

passages.quote: In my experience I was denied a job opportunity because I was the “other” sex, so women might be subjected to loss job opportunities, promotions, and we also may be paid less than our male colleagues.
passages.about: denial of job opportunity due to sex

passages.quote: I grew up near a military base, in a very diverse area, my high school had a minority rate of 62%.
passages.about: growing up near a military base and attending high school

passages.quote: There were some neighborhoods growing up that were more black and some that were more white but it wasn’t to the point where it was dangerous to go there if you were the opposite race.
passages.about: racial makeup of neighborhoods growing up

passages.quote: Then I came to UNCW, which is a primarily white institution and it really surprised me how much they lack diversity and some of the stories I have heard from people of color about how they were mistreated and how they feel like an outcast here.
passages.about: attending UNCW and hearing peers' stories of mistreatment

passages.quote: Even though where I grew up there was not a lot of racism, there was still white privilege so white people were still on top because of their race.
passages.about: observing white privilege in hometown

passages.quote: Despite always having a sense of confusion regarding my gender identity, I don’t believe I heard the term “nonbinary” until I was around fifteen years old when the famous pop singers Sam Smith and Demi Lovato came out as nonbinary to the public.
passages.about: first hearing the term nonbinary at fifteen

passages.quote: I couldn’t figure it out at the time, but the feelings I had about my gender were persistent, I felt too masculine to fit into what I thought was the standard female mold, but I didn’t feel like I was anything close to being a man either.
passages.about: feeling neither traditionally female nor male

passages.quote: It wasn’t until I was eighteen and a freshman in college that the label of “nonbinary” started to resonate with me, and at the time it made sense.
passages.about: resonating with nonbinary label in college

passages.quote: When I first started identifying publicly as nonbinary at nineteen, I assumed rather naively that the transition would be an easy one.
passages.about: identifying publicly as nonbinary at nineteen

passages.quote: I informed my social circle of my new pronouns and changed nothing else about myself.
passages.about: sharing new pronouns with friends

passages.quote: I was never maliciously misgendered by anyone, so I wasn’t too hurt when people would still refer to me as a woman, but deep down I started to feel a mounting internal pressure to change aspects of myself to fit what I thought would be the ideal image of androgyny, to be “successfully” nonbinary, and I became obsessed with this concept.
passages.about: feeling pressure to alter appearance for androgyny

passages.quote: I started dressing more masculine on purpose, even if it made me uncomfortable, shortened my name to something I thought to be more gender-neutral, and I cut my hair short.
passages.about: changing appearance and name to look masculine

passages.quote: Much to my dismay this decision proved to be a counterintuitive overcorrection, as people began to perceive my masculine gender display to be congruous with male-identification.
passages.about: people misperceiving masculine presentation as male

passages.quote: I backpedaled and regressed to a more feminine fit; I dressed the same and kept my name, but I started wearing more makeup and growing my hair out, and it had the opposite effect.
passages.about: shifting back to a more feminine look

passages.quote: Once again people assumed that the more feminine display, despite my attempts at keeping some aspects of androgyny, must have meant I identified as a woman.
passages.about: people assuming female identity from feminine display

passages.about: recovering self-image and leaving social media

passages.quote: I gained back some of my weight in muscle and became more comfortable being alone with myself and accepting my uniqueness.
passages.about: gaining muscle weight and accepting uniqueness

passages.quote: Although I was able to heal from such a dark time in my life I still deal with constant anxiety and self-esteem issues that will never really go away as long as I live presently in our society.
passages.about: continuing to deal with anxiety and self-esteem

passages.quote: I have spoken to peers who have spent hundreds of dollars on lip fillers at 17 years old and more recently a friend expressed her excitement as her breast enhancement surgery was just scheduled for the upcoming month, she is only nineteen.
passages.about: peers getting cosmetic procedures as teenagers

passages.quote: Upon reevaluating Wolf’s idea of “beauty myth” I am prompted to reflect on my time in high school.
passages.about: reflecting on high school experiences

passages.quote: My “friends” gossiped about my clothes, my skin, and my weight for the purpose of putting themselves ahead of me socially and ensuring that I would not be able to infiltrate their group, all of whom fit the mold of the “Barbie Doll” figure.
passages.about: friends gossiping about appearance to exclude student

passages.quote: I altered the way I acted by restricting my eating to change my appearance in an attempt to win over their approval.
passages.about: restricting food intake to gain peer approval

passages.quote: I recognize now that men had nothing to do will the change in my behavior, they were solely provoked by the insecurity of other women fighting for their own spots in the small social environment of our high school.
passages.about: realizing peer pressure stemmed from female peers

passages.quote: A simple change in the environment I spent my time in daily shifted my outlook on my body and image, reinforcing the idea that without the presence of societal pressure from others the beauty myth is nonexistent, or has no power over an individual.
passages.about: pandemic environment shifting body image outlook

passages.quote: Looking at me, I would say to my parents I am talkative and goofy, to my close friends that I’ve known a while I am pretty sarcastic, new friends consider me funny, my teachers would categorize me as quiet and diligent, and people I am meeting for the first time would consider me extremely quiet and potentially shy.

passages.quote: I was living with my parents and my sister and going to the same the school.
passages.about: living with family during middle and high school

passages.about: chatting with college roommate on Snapchat

passages.quote: As I moved my stuff into my room, my parents were with me, along with my roommate and her mom.
passages.about: moving into college dorm room

passages.about: friend telling a funny high school story

passages.about: laughing with friends while walking to class

passages.about: meeting another close friend in high school

passages.about: gaining a new perspective after studying Marx and Harari

passages.about: overhearing parents complain about them

passages.quote: My siblings and I always joked about how our house had “rice paper” walls.
passages.about: joking with siblings about thin walls

passages.quote: Letters came in the mail from schools and programs for troubled youth.
passages.about: receiving letters from troubled youth programs

passages.quote: I was constantly being punished for one thing or another.
passages.about: being constantly punished at home

passages.quote: Anytime me and any of my brothers bickered, my parents would automatically assume I was to blame.

passages.quote: We had citizenship sticker charts and I had the most stickers in my class.

passages.about: being on honor roll and praised by teachers

passages.quote: I knew exactly how they viewed me when private conversations were very loudly spoken just a room over (New York Italians do not know how to be quiet).
passages.about: hearing parents loudly discuss their view of them

passages.quote: My countless number of nicknames referring to my attitude problem very much reinforced the things I overheard.
passages.about: receiving nicknames about attitude problems

passages.quote: I argued, fought, yelled, screamed, and threw fits.
passages.about: acting out and throwing fits at home

passages.about: being welcomed by friends' parents

passages.quote: I am my grandparent’s favorite grandchild.
passages.about: being the grandparents' favorite grandchild

passages.quote: Nowadays, my relationship with my parents has completely changed and I am not ill behaved and a pain anymore.
passages.about: relationship with parents changing in present day

passages.about: experiencing pressures of beauty standards

passages.quote: It is extremely hard as a teenager growing up and trying to remember I don’t need to change to society’s standards but yet they are shoved in my face almost every day.
passages.about: struggling with society's standards as a teenager

passages.quote: Seeing these “perfect” girls all over my social media makes me feel like I am not “beautiful” even though the collective concept of beautiful has been altered to be an unhealthy standard for women to aspire to meet.
passages.about: feeling insecure from social media images

passages.about: facing bullying about appearance in middle school

passages.quote: I changed my hair, my clothes, my makeup, and the way I dressed to please others.
passages.about: changing appearance before entering high school

passages.about: starting to coach youth soccer in high school

passages.quote: I used to play back in middle school and the passion carried on into high school and college.
passages.about: playing soccer from middle school to college

passages.about: receiving snarky comments about coaching ability as a female

passages.quote: I was no stranger to hearing “Should we request a new team?” and “I don't think she will be as good as the male coach we had last year”.
passages.about: hearing doubts from others about female soccer coaching

passages.quote: In my very first year of coaching, I worked alongside a male counterpart.
passages.about: coaching alongside a male counterpart during first year

passages.quote: Oftentimes when at practice, the parents as well as the male children tended to flock to him.
passages.about: parents and boys favoring the male co-coach

passages.quote: Once I began to coach independently, I relayed to the parents I have previously played and coached and was adamant about having good communication with them.
passages.about: communicating experience to parents when coaching independently

passages.about: shocked by friend's assumption

passages.about: friend calling student a Fashionista demeaningly

passages.about: judgments faced at UNCW
