passages.about: friends disbelieving student was high school captain

passages.quote: My friend on campus, even being as progressive as she is, could not accept that painting my nails is a form of creativity and self expression.
passages.about: friend not accepting student's nail polish

passages.quote: Growing up in an African American household I have always asked myself that same question.
passages.about: growing up in an African American household

passages.quote: I always wondered why my dad would always give me talks about the world and how it would be a bit harder for me than white people.
passages.about: father talking to student about racial hardships

passages.quote: Or why I had to do certain things differently just so I would not get in trouble.
passages.about: having to act differently to avoid trouble

passages.quote: As a kid I did not understand any of this I would just sit there and listen.
passages.about: listening to father's talks as a kid

passages.quote: Once I started going to school that is when I started to finally develop an understanding of what he was trying to warn me about.
passages.about: starting school and understanding father's warnings

passages.quote: I started learning about things like slavery, segregation, and racism in class.
passages.about: learning about racism and slavery in school

passages.quote: Eventually I started seeing these things happen in our society today, a society that is supposed to be equal and fair to all.
passages.about: noticing racial discrimination happening in society

passages.quote: Throughout my life, in school I have always been told that ‘men are the bread winners’ and women should always look presentable for their man.
passages.about: being told gender roles in school

passages.quote: However, at home it was always the opposite, my father would tell me that man or woman, it does not matter if you are happy and at a good job it does not matter who the ‘breadwinner’ is.
passages.about: father's advice about breadwinners and careers

passages.quote: I know from personal experience that I have been catcalled.
passages.about: personal experience with being catcalled

passages.quote: My whole life I always wanted to be a CEO or own my own my business like my father did, however, people always told me that owning your own business was for men and only men could handle those jobs.
passages.about: aspirations to own a business like their father

passages.quote: My father always believed in me and wanted me to succeed in whatever I did.
passages.about: father's belief and support for student's success

passages.quote: However, down the line I decided that teacher was for me, I love teaching, children and being able to make a difference in one person’s life.
passages.about: deciding to become a teacher

passages.quote: Inside and out, they are successful in my eyes based off how they raised me, I would say my brothers and I are all extremely hard workers and will always make the most of any situation we are in, good or bad.
passages.about: being raised to be hard workers

passages.quote: Although I have taken a sociology course in High School, I have forgotten the importance of it and how extremely interesting it is.
passages.about: taking high school sociology

passages.quote: In my personal experience, I am the only straight female in my friend group, with there being only two other women.
passages.about: composition of the student's friend group

passages.quote: To start off, my guy friends basically treat me like their no strings attached girlfriend.
passages.about: guy friends treating her like a girlfriend

passages.quote: They are very flirty and make comments that as guys in a friend group, you should not be making.
passages.about: guy friends making flirty comments

passages.quote: They only do this with me and don’t do this with my other two friends who are lesbian.
passages.about: guy friends only flirting with her

passages.quote: One of my guy friends when I make a joke always has to burst out laughing, even if it isn’t the funniest thing he has heard, and says that I am “actually” really funny.
passages.about: a guy friend calling her actually funny

passages.quote: The first time he said it I didn’t mind it, but over time it gets frustrating to be seen as actually something.
passages.about: reaction to a friend's backhanded compliment

passages.quote: My guy friends are never the ones to arrange any kind of hangout unless they are getting something out of it besides just hanging out with me, or they need someone.
passages.about: guy friends rarely arranging hangouts

passages.quote: I invite them places quite frequently and so do the other girls in my friend group.
passages.about: inviting guy friends out frequently

passages.quote: Secondly, when we do hangout and aren’t up and going somewhere, they expect me to listen to all of their issues with other girls and give them advice, whether they listen or not they don’t say anything else about the discussion and they don’t even bother to ask me about my life or anything, they only care about whether something involves them or not.
passages.about: friends expecting relationship advice during hangouts

passages.quote: They will talk to me when they want something and then they don’t talk to me any other time.
passages.about: friends talking only when needing something

passages.quote: Also, they come to me begging for advice or when they need someone to talk to, but usually don’t return that kind of action back.
passages.about: friends asking for advice without reciprocation

passages.quote: In high school I went to a private Christian school where we would wear uniforms and take the most challenging courses in order to be a college preparatory school.
passages.about: attending a private Christian high school

passages.quote: All of my siblings went to high school at Asheville Christian Academy and my father served on the board.
passages.about: family attending and serving on school board

passages.quote: In a sense I did not have the choice whether I wanted to attend.
passages.about: having no choice in attending high school

passages.quote: Because I was surrounded by the same type of people in high school where we quite literally all looked the same due to the fact, we wore uniforms I think it created a stereotype in which I found myself often times having to pretend to be more Christian than I was in order to please my friend group and teachers who were very religious.
passages.about: pretending to be more religious in high school

passages.quote: For example, each Tuesday the entire high school would have a convocation and chapel.
passages.about: attending weekly school convocation and chapel

passages.quote: In order to please others, I would sing along even if I didn’t feel emotionally connected to the words or meaning of the song.
passages.about: singing along insincerely during chapel worship

passages.quote: So, in my situation my idea of the front stage was to act as if I was religious in front of my friends, family, and teachers so that I could appease them.
passages.about: acting religious to appease others

passages.quote: Before school I would need to prepare myself to act in this way so that everyone would think I was just like them.
passages.about: preparing to act religious before school

passages.quote: Now that I am in college here at the University of North Carolina Wilmington as a freshman I have experienced what I would say would be a culture shock.
passages.about: experiencing culture shock as a college freshman

passages.quote: I have met many people who are from many different backgrounds.
passages.about: meeting diverse people at college

passages.quote: Yet, there are times that I wish I could find a church group because my family always asks me about that when I come home, because I would like to please them and the standards that they have for me.
passages.about: family asking about finding a college church group

passages.quote: Here at college, I have experienced that one often gets looked down upon for being religious as from experiences with one of my friends who hates on people who are semi-religious.
passages.about: friend disliking semi-religious people at college

passages.quote: I have a couple of friends who are like me but ultimately it is difficult to find the right people, but this is by choice rather than being forced.
passages.about: having friends and finding people at college

passages.quote: Although, I do still struggle sometimes with the presentation of the self and having my identity being influenced by others, I think this in turn plays into James’ idea of the self and how we are perceived.
passages.about: struggling with presenting oneself

passages.quote: I experience this in the way that I am constantly making sure that the clothes I wear fit into what everyone else has.
passages.about: trying to fit in with clothing choices

passages.quote: The social self which is my role and reputation is seen through the lens that I want to fit in with my friends here at college and go with the flow.
passages.about: wanting to fit in with college friends

passages.quote: I feel like I am constantly worried about what people think of me and it portrays how I think of myself.
passages.about: worrying about others' perceptions of them

passages.quote: I had played plenty of sports throughout my youth and had never been scrutinized for participating because they were “boys sports” such as baseball and soccer.

passages.about: seeing sexualized women on Instagram feed

passages.quote: In my own experiences, almost every woman I have been friends with has either left or turned their back on me due to matters dealing with men.
passages.about: female friends turning on student over men

passages.quote: As for the men, I personally have seen the way that some men discuss women and their features.
passages.about: hearing men discuss and sexualize women's features

passages.quote: It is really harmful to people especially if they have insecurity’s, I would know because at the beginning of high school I was a bigger kid.

passages.quote: I would see all of these skinny girls getting hit on by the guys and I would think “I am definitely not pretty enough for guys to talk to me like that.”
passages.about: comparing self to skinny girls in high school

passages.quote: At some point, I got tired of not looking like all of these other girls so I did something about it.
passages.about: changing physical appearance to look like other girls

passages.quote: Now I get referred to as “too skinny” or “anorexic”.

passages.quote: I did not know it at the time, but I was conforming to society and going with my social group starting at a young age.
passages.about: conforming to her social group as a child

passages.about: the student was born

passages.about: the student's twin sister was born

passages.about: staying in the NICU after birth

passages.quote: Looking back at our childhood I remember the Barbie dolls and makeup she would play with.
passages.about: sister playing with Barbie dolls and makeup

passages.about: picking out hobbies at age five

passages.about: sister choosing to try dance

passages.quote: I grew up playing piano and music was just my passion, but I wanted to try baseball and see if I enjoyed sports.
passages.about: growing up playing piano and trying baseball

passages.about: talking to mom about dance intensity

passages.about: teammates and coaches making crude remarks

passages.quote: When I tried to open up to some of my friends, all they did was sit there and make fun of the things that had happened and acted like it wasn’t a big deal and that I was joking, but I wasn’t, and I realized that I could never truly open up to them.
passages.about: friends mocked student when trying to open up

passages.quote: The same thing happened with my ex-girlfriend; when I tried to let down my walls and show her the real me, she started to drift apart from me, all she wanted was for me to be the stoic, cold man that would listen to her problems and protect her, and at the time I saw nothing wrong with that.
passages.about: ex-girlfriend drifted apart when student opened up

passages.quote: Once she broke up with me, I was left with so many built-up emotions, and I had no idea what to do, so I just pushed them down with the rest because I had no idea what to do since I was supposed to be strong and emotionless.
passages.about: suppressing emotions after a breakup

passages.quote: Then one night, I was driving home from a volleyball tournament, and I was listening to a podcast, and for some reason, I started to feel; I had no idea what it was, but it was just so overwhelming, I eventually turned off the podcast and sat there for a couple of seconds in silence while that feeling was swallowing me I couldn’t understand.
passages.about: feeling overwhelmed while driving home

passages.quote: At that moment, I broke down in tears for the first time in my life.

passages.quote: I consistently wore tee shirts and athletic shorts.

passages.about: playing hazing games on high school soccer team

passages.quote: The activity was originally created as a “team bonding activity;” however the activity soon grew into a means of hazing and humiliation, particularly from the upperclassman.
passages.about: soccer team activity turning into hazing by upperclassmen

passages.quote: Over the years, the consequences created and forced onto the losers, typically lowerclassmen, became more and more outrageous, unbearable, and disgusting, mainly serving as a means of entertainment and a feeling of power for the seniors, who always conducted the activities.
passages.about: seniors forcing outrageous punishments on lowerclassmen soccer players

passages.quote: However, regardless of the punishment, members of the soccer team would almost always face up to the humiliation and degradation of the various consequences in order to feel viewed with validation.
passages.about: soccer teammates enduring humiliating punishments to gain validation

passages.quote: In contrast, members who did not face up to the consequences would frequently be regarded as “weak,” “scared,” or “unmanly,” while also frequently being harassed and targeted in future engagements of the activity.
passages.about: soccer teammates being harassed for avoiding punishments

passages.quote: Additionally, players would also encourage you after completing a consequence, saying things like, “you’re the man, I can’t believe you did that, that took guts,” further conditioning you into thinking of yourself with a false sense of validation and “manhood.”
passages.about: players validating teammates after completing hazing consequences

passages.quote: I have also noticed a large difference relating to the personality of some of my friends before and after completing their pledge process.
passages.about: noticing friends' personalities changing after fraternity pledging

passages.quote: For example, one of my friends whom I have known since high school previously used to be much more energetic, lively, and full of emotion before he decided to pledge his current fraternity.
passages.about: friend being energetic before pledging a fraternity

passages.quote: However, over the course of the process, he gradually began to develop a more careless attitude, often hiding his emotions and developing a new sense of self in order to fit in better as a man within his fraternity.
passages.about: friend becoming emotionless during fraternity pledge process

passages.quote: I personally have found evidence of this through examples including our “consequences” activity on my high school soccer team, as well as through witnessing college fraternity pledges endure humiliation in order to feel validated.
passages.about: witnessing soccer team hazing and fraternity pledges

passages.about: growing up on a farm with outdoor hobbies

passages.about: having male cousins and a younger brother

passages.quote: We would play different sports like basketball, football, and baseball.
passages.about: playing sports with family members during childhood

passages.quote: I was always just hanging out with my family and never understood these activities weren’t typically participated in by girls.
passages.about: spending childhood time doing activities with family

passages.quote: I was always wearing baggy t-shirts and athletic shorts.
passages.about: dressing in baggy clothes and athletic shorts

passages.about: childhood wardrobe preferences

passages.quote: All of my clothes were either blue, black, or grey.

passages.about: quitting the basketball team in junior year

passages.quote: As a child I was typically taking part in activities and wearing clothes that were typically reserved for boys.
passages.about: childhood clothes and activities reserved for boys

passages.about: succumbing to beauty standards during high school

passages.quote: I became obsessed with how others viewed me.
passages.about: becoming obsessed with external opinions in high school

passages.quote: I changed my hair color because I thought it would make me more desirable.
passages.about: changing hair color to appear more desirable

passages.about: not standing up against doubts about basketball skills

passages.quote: Even when I was told I shouldn’t play basketball because I didn’t look the part, I didn’t even try to disagree.

passages.quote: The number of times I was told I should dress differently eventually did drive me to changing my appearance.
passages.about: changing appearance due to repeated comments on dress

passages.about: student's physical description

passages.about: student's college major and course demographics

passages.quote: Growing up, my parents prioritized my education and taught me about my image's importance.
passages.about: parents teaching student about education and appearance

passages.quote: How that young men assume I was in the wrong class because this was Calculus 3, and what business would I have there?
passages.about: classmates questioning student being in Calculus 3

passages.quote: How older men would look at me and say, "You should smile more. It makes you look prettier."
passages.about: older men telling student to smile more

passages.about: interaction with high school teacher

passages.quote: He asked, "What do you want to be when you grow up?"
passages.about: teacher asking student about future goals

passages.quote: I responded with doctor or lawyer because I knew I wanted to have an A-list career.
passages.about: student telling teacher her career ambitions

passages.quote: His response was genuinely demoralizing, saying I should lower my standards, maybe be a teacher or a nurse, something that would suit me better.
passages.about: teacher telling student to lower career standards

passages.quote: He didn't know I was taking sophomore-level classes in 8th grade; he didn't know I had been on the Honor Roll since kindergarten; and he didn't know I was on the mathlete team.
passages.about: student's academic achievements in school

passages.quote: As a young woman, I fully developed by age 15, which meant my parents needed to warn me of how to dress and carry myself yet again.
passages.about: parents warning student about dress at fifteen

passages.quote: In elementary school, the teacher would ask, "Are there any strong boys here that can help me carry this?"
passages.about: elementary teacher asking boys for carrying help

passages.quote: Growing up and to this day, I might frequently be considered a “tomboy.”
passages.about: being considered a tomboy throughout life

passages.quote: My neighborhood was full of kids back in elementary school, and we would all hang out together after school and on the weekends.
passages.about: neighborhood kids hanging out in elementary school

passages.quote: There were more guys than girls, and I was inclined to want to do whatever the boys were doing.
passages.about: wanting to do activities with neighborhood boys

passages.quote: I was good friends with the girls, too, but making up dances and playing with barbies did not sound all that appealing to me.
passages.about: not wanting to play Barbies with girls

passages.quote: I wanted to have nerf gun wars and lightsaber fights and play video games.
passages.about: preferring Nerf wars, lightsabers, and video games

passages.quote: I don’t know if it was ever an official name that we called ourselves, but the boys and I would always hang out in this storage room at my house called The Boy’s Club.
passages.about: hanging out in The Boy's Club storage room

passages.quote: I felt cool because I was the only girl allowed in there (even though it was my house).
passages.about: being the only girl allowed in the room

passages.quote: Don’t get me wrong; there were times when I played dress-up and had the stereotypical sleepovers with my girl friends.
passages.about: playing dress-up and having sleepovers with girlfriends

passages.quote: I never felt like I would rather be a boy, but it felt more comfortable and more like me to hang with the guys.
passages.about: feeling more comfortable hanging with boys

passages.about: switching off customer service voice

passages.quote: In addition to my customer service voice, I have realized that depending on the customer, I will almost completely change my personality to match theirs, it is essentially a way for me to match their “vibe” and be able to click with them while I am ringing up their groceries.
passages.about: matching customers' personalities while cashiering

passages.about: boyfriend overheard customer service conversation

passages.quote: When I have a good interaction with a customer and I get the feeling they like me or enjoy talking to me, I feel good about myself.

passages.about: parents marrying young

passages.quote: Once my dad graduated college, that is when my parents decided to have kids.
passages.about: parents having kids after dad graduated college

passages.quote: Since I am the oldest in my family by several years, I was the most heavily impacted by this divorce, since I was an only child for quite some time.
passages.about: being heavily impacted by parents' divorce

passages.quote: Besides being difficult to come to terms with, it also has severely altered my own relationship with each of my parents.
passages.about: altered relationship with parents from divorce

passages.quote: The divorce forced me to mature at a younger age and take responsibility for me and my younger siblings, since my parents were occupied with their personal issues.
passages.about: caring for siblings during parents' divorce

passages.quote: This was definitely a challenge for me especially throughout the earlier years of my life.
passages.about: struggling during earlier life

passages.quote: An additional struggle that was introduced to me through divorce was the divorce of my grandparents.
passages.about: grandparents getting divorced

passages.quote: My grandparents have been divorced for the entirety of my life.
passages.about: grandparents being divorced whole life

passages.quote: Since my grandparents divorce was more messy and they are still not on speaking terms, they would communicate through me.
passages.about: grandparents communicating through the student

passages.quote: I had to pick and choose who I would spend time with, and was asked for my opinions on adult issues.
passages.about: handling grandparents' conflict and adult issues

passages.about: grandfather's reaction to student's nursing career plans

passages.quote: I remember almost not buying them, putting them back because I was worried the other students would think I was gay.

passages.quote: Speaking from experience, my 5-year-old nephew has told me he likes to have his nails painted.
passages.about: nephew liking to have his nails painted

passages.quote: A good example of the hegemonic masculinity that I witness with my own eyes is a multitude of my male friends who act and behave in ways that are seen or “perceived” as overtly masculine and they refuse to do anything or be associated with anything that might or would be seen or “perceived” as feminine.
passages.about: male friends acting overtly masculine

passages.quote: I have even experienced some of this hegemonic masculinity myself when I was a young boy.
passages.about: experiencing hegemonic masculinity as a boy

passages.quote: I can vividly remember getting hurt and bleeding out when I was in approximately third grade or so, and I can recall my father telling me not to cry because “crying doesn’t make it any better” as I was actively bleeding out.
passages.about: father telling student not to cry while bleeding

passages.quote: There were other instances throughout my childhood where I can remember getting hurt while playing baseball or falling off of my bike where I wouldn’t be asked if I was okay, I was told that I was okay and I was reminded that once again, crying wouldn’t make it any better and that it’d just make me feel worse.
passages.about: getting hurt and being told not to cry

passages.quote: I have some friends whose grandfather raised their son, my friends dad in this idea of being super masculine and then later on down the line, once my friends father had grown up and had a kid of his own, he raised his son the same way that his father had raised him all because he wasn’t able to “break out” of this “programming” and now all three generations think and behave in similar ways.
passages.about: friend's multi-generational family conditioning

passages.quote: I grew up in a nuclear, stereotypical household, I have two parents who are still married and one sibling, my older sister.
passages.about: growing up in a nuclear household

passages.quote: Growing up alongside my sister allowed me to realize the quirks of my parents' relationship.
passages.about: observing quirks in parents' relationship

passages.quote: My father, sister, and I all joke around and call her friends, her “fixer upper friends”.
passages.about: joking about mother's friends

passages.quote: She has lost her identity throughout the years but it started happening fast once my sister and I started transitioning out of the house for college.
passages.about: mother losing identity as daughters left for college

passages.quote: He is a handyman who spends most of his time on projects in our garage or heading out to his property he bought on the lake, building his own cabin.
passages.about: father's independent handyman activities and cabin

passages.quote: Given their personalities, my sister and I get an abnormal feeling when they go on a date night or an event by themselves.
passages.about: feeling uneasy when parents go on dates

passages.quote: My mom takes on the “traditional woman” hobbies such as keeping a clean house, going shopping for the groceries, and cooking dinner for my family.
passages.about: mother fulfilling traditional household duties

passages.quote: They come home and they cook together, they clean up together, and they carry out the same duties in the household such as laundry and cleaning.
passages.about: sister and husband sharing household chores

passages.quote: Once I reached an age to start understanding the arguments my parents had and tried to analyze them, I just believed it was mainly because my mom was annoying, not that there was an underlying concept.
passages.about: childhood perception of parents' arguments

passages.quote: My mom badgering my dad about my sister and I or why he hasn’t done something to her liking, such as leaving the garage clean, was more than those specific issues but she actually felt ignored.
passages.about: mother badgering father over family and garage chores

passages.quote: One of the first questions I was asked when enrolled into sociology was about religion.
passages.about: asked about religion in sociology class

passages.quote: I have my religious life that I do not talk about a lot and I have kept to myself since entering college then I have my social self.
passages.about: keeping religious life private in college

passages.quote: I would think about my conscious when making decisions that was deeply rooted in how my mom raised me in an extremely religious household.
passages.about: being raised in religious household

passages.quote: My religion is always used when I lose things because I always pray to St. Anthony (the saint of lost objects) when I lose things that are important to me because that is what my mom taught me.
passages.about: praying to St. Anthony for lost objects

passages.quote: I was raised in a private school where I was constantly surrounded by people, families, and a greater community that believed in the same things as me.
passages.about: attending a private religious school

passages.quote: I would see them all the time on the weekends at the same social events we would go to like brunch after church.
passages.about: seeing school community at church and brunch

passages.quote: While I had many great experiences with sports and specifically wrestling, the culture amongst the team was highly toxic and causes people to fit a mold of an ideal wrestler to be able to fit in.
passages.about: experiences with wrestling team culture

passages.quote: I wrestled for 5 years throughout my middle and high-school career.
passages.about: wrestling for five years in school

passages.quote: From 6th grade all the way up to Junior year where we had to stop due to COVID-19 restrictions.
passages.about: wrestling stopped due to COVID-19

passages.quote: Coming in I was absolutely not the ideal body type or healthy in the least bit, I had done very little physical activity before so something like this was highly out of my comfort zone.
passages.about: starting wrestling out of comfort zone

passages.quote: Immediately I was already ostracized for my weight and athletic ability.
passages.about: being ostracized by teammates

passages.quote: A vast majority of people on the team were already athletes and many people were wrestling simply to train for their other sports.
passages.about: teammates being experienced athletes

passages.quote: However I still put in the work and got to exercising.
passages.about: putting in work exercising

passages.quote: I lost around 20-30 pounds in a couple months and was getting some muscle on me towards the end of my 2nd year.
passages.about: losing weight and gaining muscle

passages.quote: However these were never things that I saw, since I was still lower in the group by comparison.
passages.about: feeling low in team hierarchy

passages.quote: The cliques were decided by athletic ability, and I constantly felt like I was falling behind.
passages.about: feeling behind in team cliques

passages.quote: Our team was winning rookie state championships, while it took me over a year to win my first match.
passages.about: taking over a year to win

passages.quote: I was winning more and more matches, getting pinned less and less, and was getting stronger.
passages.about: improving in wrestling matches

passages.quote: I wasn’t any wrestling virtuoso by any stretch, but had one of the best records on the team by my later years in high school.
passages.about: having one of the best records

passages.quote: I went from the kid who was basically an instant loss to someone who was expected to perform.
passages.about: becoming a strong performer

passages.quote: It felt amazing, I was finally making an impact on a team that I worked so hard for, and was getting respect amongst the other wrestlers.
passages.about: earning respect from teammates

passages.quote: I was assigned as one of the team captains my sophomore year, and I noticed myself acting the same way to the new kids and the captains did to me.
passages.about: becoming captain and mistreating newcomers

passages.quote: I’m not normally a very aggressive person at heart, but I took a lot of toxic masculine traits with me as I grew better at wrestling.
passages.about: adopting toxic masculine traits

passages.quote: I would basically only hang out with the other team captains, and believed I was fitting in through promoting this toxic culture that hurt me only a few years back.
passages.about: promoting toxic culture with captains

passages.quote: I would spit out phrases and insults that disgust me today, and put people down instead of picking them up.
passages.about: insulting and putting people down

passages.quote: All because I believed it would help me be a part of the “cool group”.
passages.about: trying to join cool group

passages.quote: Since I did not fit the mold of an “ideal” wrestler, I was marginalized and excluded from the group, due to me not being as good as all of the other wrestlers.
passages.about: being excluded as beginner wrestler

passages.quote: Not only was I affected from the receiving end of hegemonic masculinity, but I do admit to perpetuating these toxic norms by adapting these aggressive and competitive behaviors when I got better and better at wrestling and eventually becoming team captain.
passages.about: perpetuating toxic norms as captain

passages.quote: In my experience, I was blind to the kind of person hegemonic masculinity made me, and now being out of that environment I was able to become aware of the kind of person I was and change myself for the better.
passages.about: reflecting and changing after high school

passages.quote: I am much more in touch with my emotions, much less aggressive, and don’t fall under the exclusionary and hierarchy based groups that I was in in high school.
passages.about: current emotional state and attitudes

passages.quote: As a woman who was raised with the beauty standards that society has taught me from a young age, I actively choose to wear makeup, wear my hair nicely, and portray myself in a feminine manner.
passages.about: choosing to dress and groom in a feminine manner

passages.quote: I have experienced harassment with a member of my management team while I was working at Zaxby's back in my hometown.
passages.about: harassment by a manager at Zaxby's

passages.quote: This manager would often make sexual comments about my body, initiate unwanted physical contact, and he would often do the same to other female employees.
passages.about: manager making sexual comments and unwanted physical contact

passages.quote: We all hated when he was on shift; he made everyone feel uncomfortable, but this was such a common thing for him that no action for punishment was ever forced.
passages.about: manager making staff uncomfortable without receiving punishment

passages.quote: Most forms of harassment I have received have all been rude sexual comments; as a waitress I’ve received so many nasty comments from men that, as a young adult, are very awful to hear.
passages.about: receiving nasty sexual comments while waitressing

passages.quote: Just today as I was working, I had a man comment on my appearance and say that he was hoping that I was his waitress so he could look at me up close for a little longer while he was in the restaurant.
passages.about: restaurant customer commenting inappropriately on her appearance

passages.quote: I've had a man ask me what was in the back pocket of my jeans, and when I responded, “Why were you paying attention to my back pockets?” he replied, “Well you were flaunting it around, why can’t I look at it?”
passages.about: man making an inappropriate comment about her pockets

passages.quote: I was 16 working at my family's restaurant, bussing tables and wearing a work appropriate uniform.
passages.about: working at family restaurant when harassed at sixteen

passages.quote: She was walking down the sidewalk and a man ran up behind her and groped her breasts and crotch.
passages.about: friend being groped by a man on sidewalk

passages.quote: She was twelve years old at a Dollar General, when an older man came up to her making rude sexual comments regarding her appearance, age, and innocence.
passages.about: friend harassed by older man at Dollar General

passages.quote: I have had two times in my life when serious relationships I had been in came to an end, one way or another.
passages.about: two serious romantic breakups

passages.quote: For a couple days after these ended I remember being quite sad.
passages.about: feeling sad after relationship breakups

passages.quote: I spoke with close friends throughout in order to ground my thoughts and generate new ideas but the true sorrow I felt was not something I would ever dream of “performing”.
passages.about: talking to friends after breakups privately

passages.quote: The first is a conversation I had with a close friend of mine.
passages.about: conversation with a close friend

passages.quote: He talked about how his grandmother was recently diagnosed with a terminal illness, and how this was an event that saddened him.
passages.about: friend's grandmother diagnosed with terminal illness

passages.quote: He spoke to me about the reactions he got from others when talking about his situation with them.
passages.about: friend describing others' reactions to him

passages.quote: When I was young I lived in a big house and I thought everyone did.
passages.about: growing up in a big house

passages.quote: I went to a public school and was surprised to find out that some of my friends were not as fortunate as me when I visited their homes after school.
passages.about: visiting less fortunate friends' homes after school

passages.quote: It wasn’t until a little later in life that I realized my family was wealthy because my father was a dermatologist and my siblings and I were very privileged because of his success.
passages.about: realizing family wealth from dermatologist father

passages.quote: We had multiple cars, a nice house, were able to go on nice vacations, and eventually we were even able to go to a private school.
passages.about: family privileges and private school attendance

passages.quote: When I was told by one of my friends that my father drove a nice car because he was white, I didn’t believe him.
passages.about: friend claiming father's car was from white privilege

passages.quote: I used to work at a donut store and there were no employees who were not white.
passages.about: working at an all-white donut shop

passages.quote: But what did make me uncomfortable was when my black friend from highschool applied for a position there.
passages.about: black friend applying to the donut store

passages.quote: I thought for sure that they would hire him because he was a smart kid and could do everything I could do and I was disappointed when I found out they never called him back to come work after his interview.
passages.about: donut shop not calling back friend after interview

passages.quote: Then a week later, a white boy the same age as my friend started in the same position my friend applied and interviewed for.
passages.about: white boy hired instead of black friend

passages.quote: I left the job soon after but I always told people about what had happened.
passages.about: quitting the donut shop job

passages.quote: I answered yes to every question.
passages.about: answering yes to Peggy McIntosh privilege questions

passages.quote: Growing up I was always convinced I wanted to be a nurse because I wanted to help people.
passages.about: childhood career aspiration to be a nurse

passages.quote: However, as I grew up I gained reassurance in my designated occupational choice after educating myself on the salary an average nurse makes each year.
passages.about: learning about a nurse's salary while growing up

passages.quote: Over time, this desire to make money has overcome my admiration for the career itself.
passages.about: desire for money overtaking passion for nursing

passages.quote: My job choice has transformed into a means to make money in order to consume and enjoy the commodities of a capitalist system, such as a nice house, good food, “cool” cars, and more.
passages.about: career choice becoming solely a means to make money

passages.quote: I have experienced too many girls in my life lose confidence solely because they do not look a certain way.
passages.about: seeing girls lose confidence over beauty standards

passages.quote: I know I personally fed into the idea of beauty standards.
passages.about: personally buying into societal beauty standards

passages.quote: All around me, when I was younger and even still, each year on Halloween I see many young girls who want to be a princess for that one special night.
passages.about: seeing girls dress up as princesses on Halloween

passages.quote: Saying this from experience, there is a negative effect on young girls who are in the midst of physical and mental growth that experience these standards.
passages.about: experiencing the negative effects of beauty standards

passages.quote: Slowly time has shown to positively impact the evolving roles of gender; nevertheless, I still too often see or hear of a woman feeling less than or being treated differently than a man.
passages.about: seeing women mistreated or feeling less than men

passages.quote: In the Collective Consciousness module, I wrote about how people going against the norm is stark evidence for the collective consciousness, as many people like to feel unique.
passages.about: writing in a course module

passages.quote: Once I moved to North Carolina from New Jersey, I noticed a difference and white privilege was much more apparent.
passages.about: moving from New Jersey to North Carolina

passages.quote: My school was pretty diverse, therefore most situations felt pretty medium and was ignorant or didn’t recognize the fact I was over-privileged.
passages.about: attending a diverse school in New Jersey

passages.quote: However, once I came down to North Carolina I started to hear and see some racial stereotypes.
passages.about: hearing and seeing racial stereotypes in North Carolina

passages.quote: To be more specific, I work water rescue at the beach and all my coworkers are white males.
passages.about: working water rescue alongside all white male coworkers

passages.quote: It will encapsulate my mind all day until I wake up again the next day and see if it has changed at all.
passages.about: obsessing over morning skinniness all day

passages.quote: The beauty myth resonates so deeply with me because around a year and a half ago I went from overweight (around one hundred and fourty eight pounds for a teenage girl) to underweight (less than one hundred pounds) in less than four months.
passages.about: drastic weight loss in four months

passages.quote: My daily routine consisted of going to bed starving, waking up at noon with no energy and refusing to eat until I would have a small salad for dinner.
passages.about: unhealthy daily routine of starving and exhaustion

passages.quote: I would force myself to go for five mile runs every day no matter how tired I was.
passages.about: forcing daily five-mile runs while exhausted

passages.quote: When I would wake up in the morning I would be so lightheaded and dizzy that it would take me forever to get up and I fainted regularly.
passages.about: feeling dizzy and fainting regularly

passages.quote: Then if I ate more than I thought was “normal” I would go upstairs, turn up my music really loud, and force myself to throw up for hours until I couldn't anymore.
passages.about: forcing herself to vomit for hours

passages.quote: I did not know I was sick until I was walking downstairs one day and fainted and could not wake up.
passages.about: fainting while walking downstairs

passages.quote: My mom had to take me to the hospital and I woke up to my mom crying talking to a nutritionist.
passages.about: waking up in the hospital with her mom

passages.quote: I was later diagnosed with not only anorexia but bulimia and an excessive exercise disorder as well.
passages.about: diagnosis of anorexia, bulimia, and exercise disorder

passages.quote: I am constantly wanting to count calories and keep a track of what I am eating.
passages.about: ongoing urge to count calories

passages.quote: I still feel guilty if I do not workout every day.
passages.about: guilt when not working out daily

passages.quote: I still think about what I am going to eat everyday constantly.
passages.about: constant thoughts about food

passages.quote: I have started to exercise when I want to and do workouts I enjoy as well as appreciate some off days.
passages.about: exercising more enjoyably and taking rest days

passages.quote: In addition to this I luckily have gained a lot of weight back in a healthy way and I hope to keep practicing eating intuitively.
passages.about: gaining weight back in a healthy way

passages.quote: Being raised by immigrant parents on food stamps, it was not until my mother married my white stepfather that I understood and was made aware of the privileges of living in a higher ranking class.
passages.about: childhood raised by immigrant parents before mother's remarriage

passages.quote: Living in lower class for a few years, the constant need to make sacrifices declined mine and my family’s quality of life.
passages.about: experiencing declining quality of life in lower class

passages.quote: Our class determined the level of education I was receiving, the amount of time we would spend as a family, and our overall physical health.
passages.about: class impacts on student's education, family, and health

passages.quote: Had it not been for my mother’s new marriage, it would have been nearly impossible to move upward in class.
passages.about: mother moving upward in class through marriage

passages.quote: Fortunately, moving into a new household with a parent who is considered upper middle class gave me a headstart I lacked in my previous one; however, other institutional forces like race and gender still prevented me from receiving an equal opportunity to thrive.
passages.about: moving into an upper middle class household

passages.quote: Although my mother and I are technically apart of higher class individuals, we still suffer from discrimination due to being women of color.
passages.about: facing discrimination as women of color

passages.quote: Not only have I personally experienced the oppressing nature of class, but I have seen the effects of it on other races and genders.
passages.about: experiencing and observing class oppression

passages.quote: These circumstances have pushed me to finally begin to realize and accept my ignorance.
passages.about: realizing and accepting own ignorance about racism

passages.quote: However, I have seen acts of racism and micro-aggressions play out in front of me.
passages.about: witnessing racism and micro-aggressions

passages.quote: I also see how people, especially my close peers and family, react and interact on the topic of racism.
passages.about: peers and family reacting to racism

passages.quote: Growing up I viewed the police authorities as protectors and felt safer when they were around.
passages.about: feeling safe around police while growing up

passages.quote: When I got pulled over on a highway I was not in fear of being a subject of unexplainable brutal force.
passages.about: not fearing police brutality when pulled over

passages.quote: I often have found myself becoming a falling victim to the positive and negative impacts that technology has played throughout my life.
passages.about: feeling impacted by technology throughout life

passages.quote: I have allowed my front stage social interactions and identities to be set up to be controlled by certain factors and allow for certain actions that make me fit the “norm”.
passages.about: altering behavior to fit social norms

passages.quote: Throughout my entire life I have always been surrounded by my supportive parents, I have a great group of really close friends back at home in Charlotte and a large group of great friends at college in my fraternity, I have always played sports and loved it.
passages.about: having supportive parents, friends, fraternity, and sports

passages.quote: Yet, for the past few years till the present day, I have this empty void inside of me.
passages.about: feeling an empty void for past few years

passages.quote: I tend to fall into phases of really bad depression and forget about all of those things I just listed off.
passages.about: falling into phases of bad depression

passages.quote: When I fall into these phases, I close off all communications with my friends and family and just stay by myself and think and rot in bed for days on end.
passages.about: closing off communication and staying in bed

passages.quote: The craziest part about all of this is that I have never told a soul.
passages.about: never telling anyone about their depression

passages.quote: I put on this act that I am content with who I am and that I never have any problems, I make sure that everyone knows I am happy, so they never raise or ask any questions that I do not want to answer.
passages.about: acting content and happy around others

passages.quote: I laugh at unfunny jokes, engage in conversations that I cannot stand to listen to, it is all simply just an act for the audience.
passages.about: faking interest and laughing to keep up an act

passages.quote: There was this one night where I got invited to go bowling with all of my friends.
passages.about: getting invited to bowling with friends

passages.quote: Before that invitation, I spent the entire day in my bathroom and room doing nothing but thinking.
passages.about: spending the day alone thinking in room

passages.quote: I spoke to not a single person in my family that day and I did not want to go through any human interaction at all, especially with my friends at the time.
passages.about: avoiding speaking to family or friends that day

passages.quote: However, I overthought extremely and figured if I did not go bowling with them that they might think something is wrong and begin to question who I am.
passages.about: overthinking and deciding to attend bowling

passages.quote: So, I went.
passages.about: going bowling with friends

passages.quote: Throughout my time at the bowling alley, I was being bombarded with questions that on the inside I did not want to answer, but since I am trying to portray myself differently than how I really was at the time, I had to go along with the act and answer.
passages.about: answering questions while acting at bowling alley

passages.quote: When I would sit by myself or go to the bathroom alone, I became a completely different person than who I was while I was in front of an audience.
passages.about: dropping the act when alone at bowling alley

passages.quote: The most relieving feeling ever was when we finished, and I got back into my car, and I could officially stop putting on this act to falsely portray who I really am.
passages.about: feeling relief in car after bowling ended

passages.quote: I am such a firm believer of this concept that Goffman provided us with because I have taken part in it for years without knowing it until I learned about it in my Sociology class.
passages.about: learning about Goffman's concept in sociology class

passages.quote: In highschool, I worked with a boy who expressed his opinion that my “family must be wealthy since I’m attending UNCW”, without knowing anything about my family income.
passages.about: coworker assumed student's family was wealthy

passages.quote: The concept of ageism was first brought to my attention during a gerontology class last semester.
passages.about: learning about ageism in gerontology class

passages.quote: On the first day of class, we watched a YouTube video where younger people were asked to predict the success of older people performing certain activities such as yoga, martial arts, and running.
passages.about: watching a YouTube video in class

passages.quote: Personally, I have heard my grandmother talk about needing to get rid of wrinkles and dye her hair to look younger.
passages.about: grandmother talking about looking younger

passages.quote: This explains why in my personal experience with my grandma, she has talked about dying her hair.
passages.about: grandmother discussing dyeing her hair

passages.quote: January 18 2019, a day I will never forget, I came home from school to be greeted by my mom in the kitchen.
passages.about: coming home to find mother acting unusual

passages.quote: After more questioning she caved,not the caving where she gives a long sign and tells you because you were being annoying but the sign followed by tears, the only tears she had left in her.Cancer, a small word, powerful meaning, still to this day I don't know exactly what this word means to me.
passages.about: mother revealing father's cancer diagnosis through tears

passages.quote: My mom comes home everyday from taking my dad to yet another doctor appointment acting perfectly fine, unfazed, and my dad coming home from another agonizing session fighting the anger and exhausted with a smile.
passages.about: parents hiding distress after cancer appointments

passages.quote: I remember that each time we would hear that treatment isn't working or getting better, I prepare myself for the next day of school making sure to mask my emotions to the best of my ability.
passages.about: masking emotions at school after bad treatment news

passages.quote: Preparing for my performance at school, taking breaks between classes to sit and gather my thoughts exhausted by the end.
passages.about: taking breaks between classes to gather thoughts

passages.quote: During high school, my parents would take the time to explain to me the importance of taking higher level classes, and why—besides going to a majority white school—many of the advanced classes had little to no diversity (referring to black students).
passages.about: parents explaining advanced classes and lack of diversity

passages.quote: I would always question why I felt out of place in an AP class for example, and it took some time for me to comprehend that situation as a whole.
passages.about: feeling out of place in AP classes

passages.quote: Some teachers I’ve had in the past made me feel as if I wasn’t capable of handling the workload, which made it increasingly difficult to persuade me to go further.
passages.about: teachers doubting student's capability with workload

passages.quote: Once I had finally decided to take higher level classes, again, I felt as if I didn’t belong there.
passages.about: feeling out of place in higher-level classes

passages.quote: People have said things to me such as, “you’re the whitest black person I’ve ever met,” after I had expressed my desire to challenge myself.
passages.about: receiving racially charged remarks from peers

passages.quote: The schools I went to are placed in an upper middle class area of town.
passages.about: attending schools in an upper-middle-class area

passages.quote: We had greater access to technology and resources such as iPads and personal laptops that other schools—within the same district may I add—did not.
passages.about: having technology access at student's school

passages.quote: One person that I had met during my first year of high school described all of the threats and slurs directed towards her in particular, simply because she was wearing a Hijab to school.
passages.about: friend harassed for wearing a hijab to school

passages.quote: Born as a white American female, I have not paid much attention to a defined class.
passages.about: never paying attention to defined class

passages.quote: I have been aware that different classes existed, but I've never once referred to my lifestyle, or the lifestyle of another in forms of upper class, middle class, or lower class.
passages.about: never referring to lifestyles using class terms

passages.quote: For example, after Hurricane Florence, my house was under construction for a year.
passages.about: house repaired for a year after Hurricane Florence

passages.quote: During that period, I met a lovely construction worker named Sandro.
passages.about: meeting a construction worker named Sandro

passages.quote: I got to know him very well and that is mostly due to the fact that he Graybush 2 worked at my house every day except Sundays.
passages.about: Sandro working at the house nearly every day

passages.quote: He would arrive with his fellow employees before I would even wake up and leave right around dinner.
passages.about: Sandro's daily work schedule at the house

passages.quote: He expressed that it was tough to always be working during daylight hours and have to sacrifice time with his wife and son but his work was in order to provide for his family.
passages.about: Sandro talking about sacrificing family time for work

passages.quote: In my family beauty products are heavily used.
passages.about: family heavily using beauty products

passages.quote: Moisturizer, serums, sunscreen, toner, hair oils, fake tanner, heat protectant, hot tools, silk pillowcases, bonnets, makeup, fake lashes, and nail appointments are factored into our budget.
passages.about: beauty products factored into family budget

passages.quote: I get my nails done every two weeks which is around $70-$80 with tip and I get a bottle of tanner that costs around $30 every month or so.
passages.about: regular nail appointments and tanner expenses

passages.quote: My skincare consists of a moisturizer, 2-3 serums, sunscreen, toner, and face wash that together costs around $63.
passages.about: student's routine skincare products and cost

passages.quote: These are just a few things that I consistently buy to keep up with my beauty routine and as I get older it will only get more expensive.
passages.about: consistent beauty routine spending

passages.quote: When I am in my University 101 class, I am super talkative and really engage in the class discussions because I feel extremely comfortable to talk in this class due to the fact that it is not a class where I need to know specific details about a concept.
passages.about: acting talkative in University 101 class

passages.quote: Although I am a super talkative and an engaging person in this class, when I go to different classes I act as a completely different version of myself.
passages.about: acting differently in different college classes

passages.quote: In each separate class that I go to, I prepare a different role in my backstage to be performed in front of my many different peers and professors.
passages.about: preparing different roles for different classes

passages.quote: I prepare multiple different roles in my backstage in order to fit in to the many different class types I am enrolled in.
passages.about: adapting behavior to fit various classes

passages.quote: When I am with friends, I am a completely different person than with my family.
passages.about: acting differently with friends versus family

passages.quote: When I am around my family, I am the same person but my personality is dialed down because my family does not get me riled up as much as my friends do.
passages.about: dialing down personality when around family

passages.quote: In my backstage, when I am with friends, I typically prepare myself to be in a good mood and be goofy because that’s how we always are with each other.
passages.about: acting goofy when around friends

passages.quote: This concept also relates to when I was in high school and I played on two different softball teams; one for recreational purposes outside of my school atmosphere and one for my high school.
passages.about: playing on two different softball teams

passages.quote: When I would attend my high school teams practices, I felt as if I could fully be myself and everyone around me understood exactly who I was as a person and my personality entirely.
passages.about: feeling comfortable at high school softball practices

passages.quote: On the other hand, when I would attend practices for the other softball team I was engaging in, I felt that I needed to shut myself off due to the energy my other teammates were radiating off to me.
passages.about: shutting down at recreational softball practices

passages.quote: The comfortability I felt when playing and practicing with my high school softball team is entirely due to the roles everyone around me was putting forth to make my role feel credible.
passages.about: feeling credible on high school softball team

passages.quote: The teammates I had around me were very invested into the role I was playing, which made me feel not only credible, but also completely comfortable in the environment I was in.
passages.about: feeling comfortable with high school softball teammates

passages.quote: Unlike my high school softball team, the teammates on my recreational team outside of the school atmosphere were not fully invested in my role.
passages.about: recreational teammates not supporting the student

passages.quote: With this being said, I felt embarrassed and ashamed for not feeling credible and began to not fully play my role as they were not engaging in my role.
passages.about: feeling embarrassed during recreational softball practices

passages.quote: My mom is another great example of this phenomenon as she works for a high-end company, Gucci, and has to act a certain way when working.
passages.about: mother working at Gucci

passages.quote: In her backstage, my mom must prepare herself to be responsible and formal so she fits into the atmosphere of her work place.
passages.about: mother preparing for professional workplace atmosphere

passages.quote: After stepping outside of her office building, her role is no longer to be an employee at a job but instead to be a mother to two children.

passages.quote: My brother Benjamin was diagnosed with autism at two years old, which was the last time my parents heard him speak.
passages.about: Brother diagnosed with autism and stopped speaking

passages.quote: Since then, he has battled with his lack of motor skills, communication, sensory issues, and cognitive defects.
passages.about: Brother's ongoing struggles with autism

passages.quote: When we were little, I did not view him as a person with autism.
passages.about: Childhood perception of brother

passages.quote: As I grew up, I started to notice the effects of his disorder.
passages.about: Noticing effects of brother's autism

passages.quote: Growing up alongside my brother means that for the past 19 years, my life has been challenged every day by enduring and watching the struggles my brother and my family face because of autism.
passages.about: Growing up with an autistic brother

passages.quote: I never realized the significant impact autism has had on my brother and family until I reached my final years of high school.
passages.about: Realizing the impact of autism during high school

passages.quote: In the Hamelin household, going out to eat was something that my family has always struggled with.
passages.about: Family struggling when going out to eat

passages.quote: We would usually get takeout and eat at home but decided not to this one time.
passages.about: Deciding to dine in instead of takeout

passages.quote: One of Benjamin’s favorite places to eat is Midwood Smokehouse.
passages.about: Brother's favorite restaurant

passages.quote: Benjamin has a couple of habitual stims, which include the following: rocking back and forth, stomping, yelling, and flapping his hands excitedly.
passages.about: Brother's habitual stimming behaviors

passages.quote: In this case, he was excited to eat his favorite foods.
passages.about: Brother excited to eat at restaurant

passages.quote: As a family, we usually arrive at the restaurant around 5:30 p.m. to beat the crowds, but we did not this one time.
passages.about: Arriving late to restaurant one time

passages.quote: We are regulars, and the owners know of Benjamin and his condition and sat us in a booth in a relatively quiet area.
passages.about: Owners seating family in quiet booth

passages.quote: Unfortunately, a family was then seated behind Benjamin.
passages.about: Another family seated behind brother

passages.quote: He started to rock back and forth, shaking the backrest of the booth.
passages.about: Brother shaking booth backrest

passages.quote: My brother and I went to the same high school.
passages.about: Attending same high school as brother

passages.quote: At lunchtime, some of the special needs students would eat in the cafeteria as part of their inclusion exposure.
passages.about: Special needs students eating in cafeteria

passages.quote: The special needs teachers would accompany their students to assure their well-being.
passages.about: Teachers accompanying students in cafeteria

passages.quote: Many of them had visible disabilities such as using noise-canceling headphones, facial features, stimming, and involuntary movements.
passages.about: Visible disabilities of school peers

passages.quote: These students would usually sit together at a lunch table farther away from the typical students who would make harassing remarks, calling my brother and his classmates names such as, “retarded,” “idiots,” and “crippled.”
passages.about: Students calling brother and classmates slurs

passages.quote: From the experiences I had with my brother growing up, my family and I often feel stigmatized when we go in public with Benjamin because of his atypical characteristics and behaviors.
passages.about: Family feeling stigmatized in public

passages.quote: Restaurants are one of the difficult encounters for our family.
passages.about: Restaurant visits being difficult for family

passages.quote: We go early to avoid busy restaurant times and to avoid the stigma by having to correct his behavior and put on a performance of a typical family.
passages.about: Family dining early to avoid crowds

passages.quote: The family behind Benjamin’s side of the booth reacted to his stims and said, “Could you please stop shaking the booth and yelling?”
passages.about: Diners complaining about brother's stimming

passages.quote: Another family stared at us because of the interaction with the other family.
passages.about: Diners staring at family during confrontation

passages.quote: The teachers argue that the separation of lunch tables made my brother and his peers "easier to handle” and “less work” while still in the same room as their typical peers.
passages.about: Teachers rationalizing separate lunch seating

passages.quote: Many of my brother's classmates had stimming behaviors and other visible disabilities.
passages.about: Brother's classmates having visible disabilities

passages.quote: The special needs teachers did not do anything about the verbal harassment, allowing the discrimination to continue.
passages.about: Teachers ignoring verbal harassment

passages.quote: My brother was one of the harassed.
passages.about: Brother being harassed at school

passages.quote: I was one of the only people who told the harassers to stop their discriminatory and verbally alienating behavior toward these students.
passages.about: Student confronting cafeteria harassers

passages.quote: I was then harassed for advocating for my brother’s and his peers' role to appear credible.
passages.about: Student harassed for defending brother

passages.quote: I saw how the corrective behavior of the families in the restaurant and students in the cafeteria contribute to the effects that stigma has on those with disabilities and their families.
passages.about: Observing restaurant and cafeteria stigma

passages.quote: My parents and I struggle with Benjamin every day, trying to ensure that we, as a family, do not have to continue to face the discrimination and stigmatization that we still experience.
passages.about: Daily family struggles against discrimination

passages.quote: Instead, I look at an overall variety of women and tend to pick out certain traits, facial features, even behavioral tendencies that I compare myself to and wish that maybe I was a little different and more like them.
passages.about: comparing herself to traits of other women

passages.quote: After catching myself doing that, I attempt to snap out of that mood and realize that, yes, there is a “beauty standard” in society, but I am the most beautiful I will ever be if I just stay the way that I am naturally.
passages.about: realizing she is beautiful naturally when comparing herself

passages.quote: Through my own experiences, schools have a collective consciousness between classes by their age groups, the freshman, sophomores, juniors, and seniors.
passages.about: experience with school age group class consciousness

passages.quote: The way that I viewed myself in middle school and my first two years of high school (pre covid) was a lot lower than the way that I view myself now.
passages.about: student's past low self-perception in school

passages.quote: During this time, I did not have a lot of confidence in myself for several reasons.
passages.about: student's lack of confidence during early school years

passages.quote: In this hierarchy, I was in the middle of the spectrum.
passages.about: student's perceived popularity rank in school

passages.quote: I was not popular, but I was also not at the bottom where the weird kids resided.
passages.about: student's place on the school popularity spectrum

passages.quote: The perception of my lower position on the spectrum of popularity carried real weight and it lowered my self-esteem significantly.
passages.about: lowered self-esteem from perceived school popularity

passages.quote: I presumed that other people glanced at me and concluded that I did not meet the high standard that only popular people could live up to.
passages.about: presuming others judged student as not popular

passages.quote: I assumed people did not think the way I looked or how I acted was cool.
passages.about: assuming peers did not think student was cool

passages.quote: I thought that they thought that the way I interacted with them was uncool and weird.
passages.about: feeling perceived as uncool and weird by peers

passages.quote: Another reason for my decreased level of confidence was my perception of my own abilities as a student.
passages.about: decreased confidence from student's academic self-perception

passages.quote: All my friends took advanced classes and were in the gifted program.
passages.about: friends taking gifted and advanced classes

passages.quote: The classes I took were honors, but they were not the really tough classes my peers were taking, and they made sure to pick fun of me.
passages.about: peers teasing student for not taking tougher classes

passages.quote: When I was in 8th grade, I was taking all honors courses, except English.
passages.about: student's 8th grade course placement

passages.quote: My friends would poke fun at me for taking a “regular” class and I would laugh along with them.
passages.about: friends teasing student about taking regular English class

passages.quote: The toll that this had on me was not huge, but it did lower my confidence in my abilities as a student slightly and this weighed into my overall lower self-esteem during this time.
passages.about: teasing slightly lowering student's academic confidence

passages.quote: This combined with the perception of my rank on the popularity hierarchy resulted in myself not being able to gain a lot of confidence in myself and my abilities.
passages.about: inability to gain self-confidence during middle school

passages.quote: I thought everything I did was subpar, and I was not at the level of my classmates.
passages.about: feeling subpar compared to classmates

passages.quote: This lower perception of myself affected my confidence in my physical abilities and my social skills.
passages.about: low self-perception affecting physical and social confidence

passages.quote: I did not think I was adequately physically fit at the time and even to this day I find it hard to talk to people I respect because I think I do not have the adequate social skills to have a successful conversation with them.
passages.about: insecurities regarding fitness and ongoing social skills

passages.quote: In other words, I think that they will think that I was bad at conversation, and they will look down on me for that.
passages.about: habitual worry of being judged during conversations

passages.quote: The way I thought others perceived me in middle school and high school had no sound evidence or relevance to the objective truth of what they actually thought about me.
passages.about: reflecting on unfounded assumptions about peers' opinions

passages.quote: I shouldn’t have based my self-worth off my assumption of how other people thought about me because those assumptions could have been completely inaccurate.
passages.about: reflecting on basing past self-worth on assumptions

passages.quote: When my friends made fun of me for taking easier classes than they were, I interpreted this as them thinking that I am actually less intelligent and cannot handle the workload of a higher-level class.
passages.about: interpreting friends' teasing as judgment of intelligence

passages.quote: Knowing what I know today, the assumption I made of my friends thinking I was less intelligent was completely false because they explained to me that it was false a few years ago.
passages.about: friends clarifying their past comments to student

passages.quote: Even though my assumptions of my friend's beliefs towards my intelligence were wrong, it still had a dramatic impact on my self- esteem and overall ability to reach my full potential in school at that time.
passages.about: past assumptions impacting student's self-esteem and schoolwork

passages.quote: In middle school and high school, my full potential was not reached because I allowed false assumptions about my intelligence and my popularity, diminish my confidence.
passages.about: false assumptions diminishing student's confidence in school

passages.quote: I personally know many men who have been shamed and/or kicked out of their family/society because they decided to be who they want to be.
passages.about: men shamed or kicked out by families

passages.about: reactions to student painting their nails black

passages.about: buying her 15-year-old car off a used lot

passages.quote: The house she lives in is a ranch, which just so happens to be one of the smallest among the mansions in the expensive part of town.
passages.about: living in a small ranch among mansions

passages.quote: I am from a middle-class family, who happens to reside among upper-class families.
passages.about: belonging to a middle-class family among wealthy neighbors

passages.quote: We all played tag on the playground, laughed together, and probably drove our teachers crazy.
passages.about: playing together during elementary school years

passages.about: mother losing her marketing director job

passages.quote: My father is self-employed, so her benefits through the company she worked for covered my entire family.
passages.about: relying on mother's job for family health benefits

passages.about: mother waiting on hold for Obamacare application

passages.about: classmates questioning her reusing an old backpack

passages.quote: I would lie and say that I did not like any of the new patterns.
passages.about: lying to peers about not liking new backpack patterns

passages.quote: My mom and dad did everything they could to provide my brother and me with everything we wanted for Christmas that year by putting it on a credit card.
passages.about: parents charging Christmas gifts on credit cards

passages.quote: When my mom lost her job, my family, a middle-class family, endured a healthcare gap.
passages.about: family enduring a healthcare gap after job loss

passages.quote: In my childhood I had a best friend who was also my next door neighbor.
passages.about: having a childhood male best friend next door

passages.quote: In second grade we decided to play church league basketball, we had no idea we wouldn’t be on the same team and would end up playing against each other, but in the end that turned out to be a blessing.
passages.about: playing church league basketball in second grade

passages.quote: Being young and ignorant I thought it was because they thought I was cute and they liked me, but then I asked one of them why they always wanted to scrimmage me and he told me it was because I am a girl so I’m not as good and easier to play against.
passages.about: facing gender discrimination during basketball scrimmage

passages.quote: I owned camouflage everything, I would shoot my BB guns in the backyard with my dad aiming at targets and squirrels.
passages.about: being a tomboy and shooting BB guns

passages.quote: I also learned in class from my peers that camouflage and guns weren’t lady-like and that I should act more like a girl.
passages.about: peers criticizing her tomboy interests in fifth grade

passages.quote: So I got rid of all of my camouflage and I put up my guns and started doing girlier things.
passages.about: changing interests to be more girly due to peer pressure

passages.quote: By the time I had reached my sophomore year of high school I had stopped caring about what other people thought about me, the way I acted, and the way I dressed.
passages.about: stopping caring about other people's opinions in high school

passages.quote: I had a boyfriend at the time and he felt as though he needed to have a say in who I hung out with, who I talked to, what I wore, and where I went.
passages.about: being in a controlling high school relationship

passages.quote: I was granted the raise, but later found out about the sexual things my boss had said about me to other male workers, and his thoughts on my body are the main reason I even got the raise.

passages.about: carrying a taser for personal safety

passages.about: personal body image insecurities

passages.quote: Oftentimes I ask what makes them say that, and the answers vary, but there's always three constants: makeup, hair style, and clothing choice.
