passages.quote: Growing up in a middle-to-upper class in America, I have experienced different social standards from people.
passages.about: experiencing social standards in middle-to-upper class

passages.quote: I always partook in beauty pageants, was cheer captain and dated the star football player, as well as drove a nice vehicle once I turned sixteen.
passages.about: high school activities and social life

passages.quote: Little do they know that I look down upon myself most days and do not see the “beauty” that I was nominated for in all of those pageants I did as a child and into my teenage years.
passages.about: personal insecurity despite doing beauty pageants

passages.quote: As a young woman growing up, I always battled with the boys in different and unique ways.
passages.about: competing with boys while growing up

passages.quote: Along with my experiences of beauty pageants and cheerleading, I also played basketball.
passages.about: participating in pageants, cheerleading, and basketball

passages.quote: However, I tried to bend those standards and boost the confidence of other young women around me to try something different, like playing a boys sport.
passages.about: encouraging other girls to play sports

passages.quote: Throughout my years going through middle school and highschool I was a competitive cheerleader for almost 10 years.
passages.about: cheering competitively for almost ten years

passages.quote: When tryouts came around I always got super nervous because I always felt well I'm not good enough, I'm not strong enough, I do not have the tumbling or stunting skills I needed to have to be on the team I really wanted to make.
passages.about: feeling nervous and inadequate during cheer tryouts

passages.quote: After many tryouts of still not making the team I just brought myself down and felt like everything thought of me as she's not good enough for this team.
passages.about: feeling defeated after failing tryouts

passages.quote: Many times throughout my cheer career I have been told you just do not have the skills you need to make this team, or you just aren't the right fit for this team yet.
passages.about: being told she lacked necessary cheer skills

passages.quote: Throughout practices we would get switched out of our spots in the routine and be replaced by others on the team because they were”better” at it than me.
passages.about: getting replaced by others during practices

passages.quote: One day at practice our coach was helping us work on a stunt, yet again we couldn't make the stunt hit like it needed to so I got taken out and replaced by one of the boys.
passages.about: being replaced by a boy during practice

passages.quote: I would talk to my friends at practice who were girls and they always told me do not worry about it, you are just as good as everyone else, that made me feel better but I was still always defeated knowing a boy took my spot in parts of the routine because they were stronger or better at my position.
passages.about: female friends comforting her about cheer spots

passages.quote: During many cheer practices I felt my coach would just make quick assumptions about my ability to complete the skills that needed to be completed.
passages.about: coach making assumptions about her abilities

passages.quote: I came across this beauty myth standard when I was a competitive cheerleader and there were also boys on my team which made it hard.
passages.about: experiencing standards while cheering with boys

passages.about: student's parents' professions

passages.about: student's family home and schooling

passages.about: working as a college swim instructor

passages.quote: I have had perfectly good children with controlling or judgemental parents that ruin the whole lesson.
passages.about: dealing with difficult parents during lessons

passages.quote: My boss tells me that once I put my instructor shirt on, I have the power.
passages.about: advice received from swim instructor boss

passages.quote: Having now been teaching for a few months, I know the flow and rhythm of the lesson and am confident in my ability to teach.
passages.about: gaining confidence teaching swim lessons

passages.about: a young girl arriving for swim lesson

passages.about: a mother taking over the swim lesson

passages.quote: It was overall a disastrous and pointless lesson for everyone involved.

passages.quote: With these expectations in place, it was shocking and uncomfortable when the mother came into the water and started teaching the child.
passages.about: discomfort when mother entered pool

passages.about: mother disrupting student's role as instructor

passages.quote: The mom and child came back the next weekend for a second lesson.
passages.about: mother and child returning for another lesson

passages.quote: I was able to change my role and teach the mom how to teach the child.
passages.about: adjusting teaching strategy for mother and child

passages.about: working at a restaurant since age 16

passages.about: dress code when starting as a hostess

passages.quote: I would wear dresses, skirts, and of course, makeup.
passages.about: wearing dresses and makeup to work

passages.quote: There was never much of a problem with anyone underdressing, but if someone was wearing something scandalous, you could expect one of the older female workers to say something about it.
passages.about: older female coworkers criticizing scandalous clothing

passages.quote: The male managers would never say anything about the hostesses skirts being too short, an inch of their stomach showing, or their tops being low cut, but they would stare.
passages.about: male managers staring at hostesses

passages.quote: Other female coworkers, especially the waitresses, really had a hand in how we were supposed to look, and when I got moved up to a waitress, as the youngest one, I followed their lead.
passages.about: becoming a waitress and following coworkers' appearance standards

passages.quote: At one point about a year ago, I mainly stopped wearing makeup in my everyday life, but every time I worked, I put makeup on.
passages.about: wearing makeup only for restaurant shifts

passages.quote: A few times I worked, I forgot my big hoop earrings, and I would actually make less money at work.
passages.about: earning less money when forgetting hoop earrings

passages.quote: I have never worn my glasses to work, as I didn’t feel comfortable doing so.
passages.about: avoiding wearing glasses at work

passages.quote: We were prone to being more sexualized and hit on as hostesses, the youngest workers in the building, by much older coworkers and bosses, than in any other position.
passages.about: hostesses being sexualized by older bosses and coworkers

passages.quote: Because of this, hostesses were often put in competition with other female coworkers, as the beauty myth describes, when other female coworkers would scrutinize our outfits when we dressed too provocatively.
passages.about: female coworkers scrutinizing hostesses' provocative outfits

passages.quote: I’ve witnessed both sides of this, being a waitress and a hostess, and putting women down because of the competition of the beauty myth only allowed the men that worked there more control and power over us, and benefited them more.
passages.about: witnessing workplace competition between waitresses and hostesses

passages.quote: Male employees and managers would look or stare at young girls who fit the beauty myth sexually, objectifying them and enjoying what the beauty myth demands from young women.
passages.about: male staff staring sexually at young workers

passages.quote: I have forgotten earrings before, made less money, and chastised myself because I didn’t fit the beauty myth well enough, so I was less valued and less beautiful.
passages.about: chastising oneself after earning less without earrings

passages.quote: At the very beginning of the semester, our class studied the very beginnings of the human consciousness and concept of “the self,” and how oftentimes we are influenced and lifted up by the communities around us.
passages.about: class studying human consciousness earlier in semester

passages.quote: Growing up my parents made sure we had everything.
passages.about: parents providing for the student growing up

passages.quote: Growing up my dad could never be home because he was always working.
passages.about: father always working and away from home

passages.quote: At no fault to him, I remember days when I was little where I would go a few days without actually seeing my dad.

passages.quote: He would work from sun up to sun down, he left before I would wake up for school, and some days I’d be in bed asleep before he got home.

passages.quote: It was the end of my junior year of high school before I even realized how much time I lost with my dad, and around that time he realized I was actually smart.

passages.quote: I feel as though every time I look at my E-bill there are more and more random charges I have no idea what they’re for.

passages.quote: While I have never actually met someone with generational wealth, I have met and had to be around people, teenagers, of the upper class.
passages.about: interacting with upper-class teenagers

passages.quote: I grew up in Lexington, South Carolina, I went to the newest middle school and high school in the area at the time.
passages.about: growing up and attending school in South Carolina

passages.quote: I knew and hung out with a lot of people who lived below their means, amazing people they are.
passages.about: hanging out with peers living below their means

passages.quote: I also hung out with people who did not have a care in the world about money.
passages.about: hanging out with wealthy, careless friends

passages.quote: I can notice that people will treat me just slightly differently when I am wearing makeup and dressed nicely compared to when I am not and am wearing more relaxed clothing.

passages.quote: One day when I went in wearing a put together outfit and wearing makeup, the man behind the counter told me I was too beautiful to pay.

passages.quote: The next day I went in wearing no makeup and just a t-shirt.
passages.about: paying for coffee without makeup

passages.quote: Growing up as a female in 21st century America, I have seen impossible beauty standards be created and perpetuated in an endless loop.

passages.quote: Social media has only furthered this problem, I first remember noticing the issue in middle school when I began accessing technology along with my peers.
passages.about: noticing beauty standards on technology in middle school

passages.quote: As a person who identifies as non-binary, but is a female at birth and feminine presenting, it is a daily struggle to express how even though I may look like a girl, I do not feel like one nor identify as one.
passages.about: identifying as non-binary while feminine presenting

passages.quote: Abiding to these roles may seem easy, but transphobic and homophobic comments from society can make it extremely hard to feel comfortable within my own skin.
passages.about: feeling uncomfortable due to transphobic and homophobic comments

passages.quote: For my first two years of high school, I lived in the diverse and blue-collar town of Cedar Rapids, Iowa.
passages.about: living in Cedar Rapids during high school

passages.quote: As an Advanced Placement (AP) student, I was surrounded by white upperclassmen.
passages.about: being surrounded by white upperclassmen in AP

passages.quote: During my sophomore year, I was enrolled in five AP classes.
passages.about: taking five AP classes sophomore year

passages.quote: There was a total of four people of color in my classes, collectively.
passages.about: having few people of color in AP classes

passages.quote: In my AP Biology class, I was one of three girls.
passages.about: being one of three girls in biology

passages.quote: In eighth grade, I was in a program with only twenty other middle school students from around the entire county that allowed us to take honors biology at our future high school.
passages.about: taking high school honors biology in eighth grade

passages.quote: Following eighth grade, I took honors chemistry and honors environmental science during my freshman year.
passages.about: taking honors science classes during freshman year

passages.quote: Despite my qualifications; in labs and during group work, my male classmates assumed that I was incompetent by the way that I looked.
passages.about: male classmates assuming she was incompetent

passages.quote: On lab days, I drug my feet to class.
passages.about: dreading lab days in science class

passages.quote: It made my stomach churn with anxiety walking to fifth period each day.
passages.about: feeling anxious walking to fifth period

passages.quote: My uniform of choice in high school was light-colored dresses and skirts.

passages.about: taking medication at different life points

passages.quote: Additionally, I am a Criminology major and plan to work in Victim Advocacy in the future.
passages.about: current college major and career plans

passages.quote: This reminds me of when I first began seeing the signs that my mother had bipolar disorder II, I was just nearing my last years of high school, I had never seen any other signs or even known about the illness.
passages.about: noticing mother's bipolar disorder signs in high school

passages.quote: I experienced lots of emotions when I found out she was suffering, and I was really the only main one there for her, I didn’t know what would come.
passages.about: supporting mother after finding out about her illness

passages.quote: I remember I had to either involuntarily commit her, or there would be worse consequences in the justice system, for the first time at just 16 years old.
passages.about: involuntarily committing mother at age sixteen

passages.quote: I heard the cop in the background talking bad about my mother and how he knew her in the past, displaying the same awful stigma that most law enforcement leads with.
passages.about: hearing a police officer disparage their mother

passages.quote: Another moment when we began arguing a lot, I felt like it was because she wasn’t herself, but she told me “I’m the same, I have always been this way”; this made me come to the realization that I too was making her into the disorder herself and not seeing who she really is.
passages.about: arguing with mother about her behavior and disorder

passages.quote: It hit me like a truck, just as it does for lots of families in society, especially because I have a little brother that was too young to understand, and I had no idea how to explain it to him.
passages.about: struggling to explain mother's illness to little brother

passages.quote: I bottled all my emotions in, and I didn't want to talk to anyone, no one understood, and I was going through my own battle during all of this all alone, but she is my mom.
passages.about: suppressing emotions while dealing with mother's condition alone

passages.quote: My mom takes care of herself for the most part, but there are times when this is needed.
passages.about: mother occasionally needing caregiving support

passages.quote: I have seen my mom go through many health evaluations until they settled on Latuda.
passages.about: mother undergoing evaluations before starting Latuda

passages.quote: The only thing about this medicine is that she's been taking it for over 10 years and if it gets out of her system, she will most likely have a manic episode.
passages.about: mother taking Latuda for over ten years

passages.quote: Often, I would go without talking to her and had to stop by her house to check on her.
passages.about: stopping by mother's house to check on her

passages.quote: One thing she thought was that all the electronics were bad, she was being tracked.
passages.about: mother believing electronics were tracking her

passages.quote: It saddened me when she would see me as the enemy or think that things were happening that weren't.
passages.about: feeling sad when mother viewed them as enemy

passages.quote: Sometimes I would have no idea where my mom was, I would have to look for her, who was going to be there for her.
passages.about: searching for mother when she went missing

passages.quote: All while I was trying to establish my life and finish college.
passages.about: trying to finish college during family difficulties

passages.quote: Her childhood was very tough, and her siblings were not close, their mother and father also suffered from their own mental illness.
passages.about: mother's difficult childhood and family mental illnesses

passages.quote: My mom is also the only child that helps my grandmother with her mental disorder.
passages.about: mother caring for grandmother with mental disorder

passages.quote: Today, my mom is doing great, she is still here improving her life for the better, in a good area.
passages.about: mother doing well and living in good area

passages.quote: As a woman in this society, I run into many obstacles related to my health and have to make decisions or deny “help” to better my health.
passages.about: facing obstacles in healthcare decisions

passages.quote: I work as a server in a local restaurant, and oftentimes when I go to greet a table, everyone at the table is on their phones.
passages.about: customers on phones while dining

passages.quote: I’m on my phone more than I like, but throughout the entire dining experience, everyone is on their phones rather than talking.
passages.about: personal phone use habit

passages.quote: I am from Pittsburgh and was born and raised in Burrell, about 30 minutes North East of the main city before moving to NC in 2015.
passages.about: growing up near Pittsburgh and moving to North Carolina

passages.quote: I was younger, about twelve, when I moved but I still remember all the memories I have of the city and the surrounding areas.
passages.about: moving at age twelve and remembering the area

passages.quote: To make a very long story short, my dad passed away my senior year of high school in 2021 after a battle with ALS.
passages.about: father passing away from ALS in 2021

passages.quote: People would always ask me how he was doing, how I am doing or my mom, sister, etc.
passages.about: people asking about student's family during father's illness

passages.quote: I would always just lie because it was hard to talk about.
passages.about: lying about family struggles when asked by others

passages.quote: I have been exposed to depression in my life with my dad and my sister following his passing, but reading a bit about your experience shows how everyone battles things differently.
passages.about: father and sister experiencing depression after his death

passages.quote: These frustrating moments throughout Engelman’s story reminded me of how my dad gets frustrated with my grandfather because he hides his TV remote and money and forgets where he puts them, so he assumes someone stole his items.
passages.about: father's frustration with grandfather's forgetfulness

passages.quote: When my dad tries to help, my grandfather won’t tell him much and gets agitated and hangs up the phone.
passages.about: grandfather hanging up phone when dad tries to help

passages.quote: This is very tolling on my dad because he has a full-time job and a family to provide for while having to deal with these frustrating situations over the phone.
passages.about: stress of caregiving over phone on student's dad

passages.quote: My grandfather stays in Ohio while we live in North Carolina, but luckily my dad’s sister lives up there, so he can coordinate with her when he needs additional help.
passages.about: family locations and coordination of care

passages.quote: Like Engelman, when he would receive phone calls from Doug, I see it within my dad that same expression of whether it’s good news or another problem to solve.
passages.about: observing father's expressions during phone calls

passages.quote: That really connects with what I’ve seen between my dad and my grandfather.
passages.about: observing interactions between dad and grandfather

passages.quote: When my grandfather calls in a confused or angry state, my dad tries to calm him down, but sometimes he loses patience.
passages.about: dad calming confused grandfather over the phone

passages.quote: I have also seen it in person once when we were visiting him because while in his room he was talking about some man that gets into fights with and out of nowhere, he goes” he is standing right there” but there was no one there.
passages.about: visiting grandfather who hallucinated a man in room

passages.quote: Just like Engelman with Doug my dad had to figure out how to approach in which in this situation my dad moved the door which the shadow from the light was gone and my grandfather then replied, “he’s gone, where did he go”.
passages.about: dad moving door to dispel grandfather's hallucination

passages.quote: Being able to personally connect to Engelmans story has made me realize how my dad’s life has changed since becoming the primary caregiver of my grandfather.
passages.about: dad's life changes since becoming primary caregiver

passages.quote: He has become more patient but also compassionate not just toward my grandfather but others as well.
passages.about: dad becoming more patient and compassionate

passages.quote: After reading A Boy Broken and having Engelman as my sociology of mental disorders professor, it gives me a new understanding of the class and mental disorders.
passages.about: having the book's author as a professor

passages.quote: One personal example of where I believe that it was ok for me to lie was when I was babysitting.
passages.about: babysitting experience where they lied

passages.quote: The little girl and I were painting together, and she asked me if her painting she made of her and her parents was good (it was not).
passages.about: child asked opinion on bad painting

passages.quote: I obviously lied and said yes because why would you tell a little girl that her painting was not the best?
passages.about: complimented a child's bad painting

passages.quote: I lost my brother in 2020 and my dad in 2021, and there is so much I went through that I can use to help others in the future.
passages.about: brother and father died in 2020 and 2021

passages.quote: My father was killed, and when my brother died, I kind of fell apart.
passages.about: father was killed and brother died

passages.quote: Through my own experience, I have noticed that the majority of my friends who live with single parents live with their mothers.
passages.about: friends living with single mothers
